Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P35_02",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis specification describes the functionality,\nAPI\nand the configuration for the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Diagnostic Management (DM).\nThe\nDM\nis an\nUDS\ndiagnostic implementation according to ISO 14229-1[1] and a\nSOVD\nimplementation according\nASAM\nSOVD v 1.0.0 [2] for the Autosar Adaptive Platform.\n1.1 Diagnostic interface\nSince release R19-03 a C++ interface was introduced for diagnostics as a replacement\nfor the former ara::com based service interface.\n1.2 AUTOSAR Diagnostic Extract Template (DEXT)\nThe AUTOSAR Diagnostic Extract Template (DEXT) [3] is the configuration input to the\nDM\n.\n1.3 Software Cluster\nThe AUTOSAR adaptive platform is able to be extended with new software packages\nwithout re-flashing the entire\nECU\n. The individual software packages are described by\nSoftwareClusters\n. To support the current approaches of diagnostic management\n(like software updates), each\nSoftwareCluster\nhave its own DiagnosticAddresses.\nThe\nDM\nis intended to support an own diagnostic server instance per installed\nSoft-\nwareCluster\n. All diagnostic server instances share a single TransportLayer instance\n(e.g. DoIP on TCP/IP port 13400).\n1.3.1 Diagnostic Server\nThe\nDiagnostic Communication Management\nresponse handling basically re-\nsembles the functionality of the\nDcm BSW\nmodule of the AUTOSAR Classic platform.\nI.e. it is responsible for processing/dispatching of diagnostic services according to ISO\n14229-1[1] and\nSOVD\nservices as per Service-Oriented Vehicle Diagnostics standard\nSpecification [2]. That means:\n\u000f\nReceiving diagnostic request messages from the network layer.\n\nUDS DoIP\nor proprietary transport protocol requests\n\nSOVD HTTP\n/\nREST\nrequests\n35 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P39_03",

    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nspecification shall be considered as an additional and required specification for imple-\nmentation of\nDiagnostic Management\n.\n45 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters in\nthe AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the interfaces\nprovided by\nDiagnostic Management\nto other Functional Clusters. Section 5.2 \nRequired Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nDiagnostic Management\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [7].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Table 6.1: RequirementsTracing\n6.1 Not applicable requirements\n[SWS_DM_NA]\n{DRAFT}\nd\nThese requirements are not applicable as they are not within\nthe scope of this release.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04059, RS_Diag_04171, RS_Diag_04195, RS_-\nDiag_04200, RS_Diag_04218)\n71 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P73_110",
      "source_element": "SWS_DM_01571",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 73,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.1: Component view on Diagnostic Management\n7.1 Functional cluster life-cycle\nThis chapter handles the diagnostics functional cluster lifecycle. It describes the be-\nhavior of the diagnostic daemon in several cases, like startup, shutdown or crash. In\nthese cases the interaction with the application and diag\nAPI\nlibrary is also described.\nThis chapter defines requirements, which are related to the lifecycle of the diagnostic\nfunctional cluster. It will describe the startup and shutdown procedure of the\nDM\n.\n7.1.1 Startup\nThe startup procedure of the\nDM\nis treated as vendor-specific.\n[SWS_DM_01571]\n{DRAFT}\nLoad persisted data\nd\nOn a\nDM\nstartup trigger from\nExe-\ncution Management\n,\nDM\nshall restore all data, which was persisted from persistent\nmemory.\nc\n(SWS_CORE_10001)\n7.1.2 Shutdown\nIn the following the required shutdown procedure of the\nDM\ndaemon is defined.\n73 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P74_111",
      "source_element": "SWS_DM_01572",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 74,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIt is expected, that during a synchronized/orchestrated shutdown applications, which\nare interacting with the\nDM\n, are already shutdown before the\nDM\ndaemon is requested\nto be shutdown by the\nExecution Management\n.\n[SWS_DM_01572]\n{DRAFT}\nGraceful shutdown\nd\nOn a\nDM\ntermination trigger from\nExecution Management\n,\nDM\nshall gracefully shutdown itself.\nc\n(SWS_CORE_10002)\n[SWS_DM_01573]\n{DRAFT}\nStop all running\nTransport Protocol Handler\ns\nd\nOn a\nDM\ntermination trigger from\nExecution Management\n,\nDM\nshall call\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Stop\non all\nstarted UdsTransportProtocolHandlers.\nc\n(SWS_CORE_10002)\n[SWS_DM_01574]\n{DRAFT}\nWrite data to be persisted\nd\nLatest on a\nDM\ntermination\ntrigger from\nExecution Management\n,\nDM\nshall write all data, which has the need of\npersistent storage, to persistent memory.\nc\n(SWS_CORE_10002)\n7.1.3 Daemon crash\nIn case the\nDM\ndaemon crashes for some reason, it will as most as possible be restarted\n\"silently\", so that the adaptive applications can still run without a restart.\nIn chapter \" 7.4.4.1\" the caching for DEM related features is described to be able to\nre-sync after a daemon restart.\n[SWS_DM_01580]\n{DRAFT}\nd\nThe DCM related parts shall behave like a session\ntimeout according to [SWS_DM_00381] or priority handling in [SWS_DM_00427],\n[SWS_DM_00428], [SWS_DM_00429], and [SWS_DM_00430] in a conversation.\nc\n()\n7.2 UDS Transport Layer\nSince there exist standardized as well as OEM specific\nUDS\nTransport Layers, the\nDM\nsupports a standardized C++ API (called\nTransport Protocol API\n), where differ-\nent kinds of\nUDS\nTransport Layers can be connected. Currently the Adaptive Platform\nonly provides a detailed description of Ethernet-based network technologies, which\nmandates support of\nDoIP\n[5]. It is very likely, that upcoming releases of the\nDM\nwill\nalso detail CAN, CAN-FD, FR, ... networks. The\nTransport Protocol API\nallows\nfor extensions of\nDM\ntowards not-yet-detailed and proprietary\nUDS\nTransport Protocols.\n[SWS_DM_00342]\n{DRAFT}\nIndication of UDS message reception\nd\nUDS\nTransport Protocol\nimplementation shall call\nara::diag::uds_transport::\nUdsTransportProtocolMgr::IndicateMessage\non its\nara::diag::uds_-\ntransport::UdsTransportProtocolMgr\nreference ((see [SWS_DM_00330])),\nas soon as it has at least the following information of an incoming\nUDS\nrequest avail-\nable:\n\u000f\nUDS\nsource address\nof the request.\n74 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P75_112",
      "source_element": "SWS_DM_00386",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 75,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nUDS\ntarget address\nof the request.\n\u000f\nType of the UDS target address (physical or functional)\n\u000f\nSize of the entire UDS message starting from SID\n\u000f\nIf the\nUDS\npayload is larger than 1 byte, at least two bytes are received and shall\nbe forwarded in the parameter\npayloadInfo\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\nThe\nUDS\nTransport Protocol (TP) implementation can optionally provide the so far re-\nceived\nUDS\nmessage content in\npayloadInfo\n. It is up to the TP implementation to\ndecide how much of the so far received data is provided. It is recommended to provide\nat least the first two bytes of the received message. The\nDM\nis then able to detect a\nfunctional received tester present (UDS bypass logic) and accept this message, even\nthe\nDM\nis currently processing a physical request. If the TP does not provide any data\nin\npayloadInfo\n, the\nDM\nwill not be able to detect the functional TP and will reject\nthe message reception in\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProto-\ncolMgr::IndicateMessage\n(see also [SWS_DM_00386]). This might or might not\nresult to failures on the TP. E.g.\nDoIP\nprovides 'Negative Acknowledge' (NACK) codes\nin that case, while CAN (Controller Area Network) does not have any TP failures.\n7.2.1 Support of proprietary UDS Transport Layer\nThe UDS Transport Protocol API is formally described in section B.1. This section de-\nscribes the required interaction of the components using this API. Each (proprietary)\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation subclasses the abstract class\nara::\ndiag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler\n, which shall be pro-\nvided by\nDM\naccording to [SWS_DM_00315].\n7.2.1.1 Initialization, Starting and Stopping of a proprietary UDS TransportLayer\n[SWS_DM_00329]\n{DRAFT}\nLifecycle management of an\nUDS Transport Pro-\ntocol\nimplementation\nd\nThe lifecycle of an\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplemen-\ntation shall be managed by the\nDM\nin the following order:\n\u000f\nCreation of the\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation by calling its\nconstructor\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHan-\ndler::UdsTransportProtocolHandler\n.\n\u000f\nInitializing of the\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation by calling\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::\nInitialize\n.\n\u000f\nStarting of the\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation by calling\nara::\ndiag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Start\n.\n75 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },

      "source_page": 76,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nStopping of the\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation by calling\nara::\ndiag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Stop\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00330]\n{DRAFT}\nConstruction of an\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimple-\nmentation\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall by\nDM\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00331]\n{DRAFT}\nInitialization of an\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimple-\nmentation\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall call returned\nkInitializeOk\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_01745]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior on failed transport protocol initialization\nd\nIf a\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Ini-\ntialize\nreturns\nkInitializeFailed\n, the DM shall stop the initialization process of\nthe transport protocol and call no further methods on that\nara::diag::uds_trans-\nport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_01744]\n{DRAFT}\nProcessing of ChannelReestablished\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall\nprocess a call of\nara::diag::uds_transport::\nUdsTransportProtocolHandler::Start\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_01743]\n{DRAFT}\nRequire a started UdsTransportProtocolHandler\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall call\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHan-\ndler::Transmit\nand\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProto-\ncolHandler::Stop\nonly after\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransport-\nProtocolHandler::Start\nwas called.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00332]\n{DRAFT}\nStarting of an\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplemen-\ntation\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall call the\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransport-\nProtocolHandler::Start\nmethod of the\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplemen-\ntation during startup/initialization phase, before reporting\nApplicationState.-\nkRunning\nto the execution management and after call to\nara::diag::uds_-\ntransport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Initialize\nhas returned.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n76 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "source_page": 77,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01742]\n{DRAFT}\nAsynchronous UDS protocol start\nd\nThe\nara::\ndiag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Start\nimplemen-\ntation shall be asynchronous and can continue starting the\nUDS\nprotocol handler after\nthe call has       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00351]\n{DRAFT}\nConfirmation Result\nd\nWhen the the network layer was\nable to send the UDS response message to the network, the\nresult\nargument in\nthe\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolMgr::Transmit-\nConfirmation\nshall be set to\nkTransmitOk\n, otherwise to\nkTransmitFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n7.2.1.4 Channel Notifications\nEach incoming UDS request message is assigned an exact\nUDS Transport Pro-\ntocol\nimplementation specific\nChannel\n. With the normal request/reply paradigm in\ndiagnostics, the UDS response message is sent out at the same\nChannel\n, from which\nthe UDS request has been received. Therefore the\nChannel\nidentifier is given to\nthe\nDM\nin\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolMgr::Indi-\ncateMessage\nin the form of parameter\nglobalChannelId\n. The UDS service for ECU reset is a candidate for such a requirement.\nThe upcoming requirements shall cover this use case.\n[SWS_DM_00356]\n{DRAFT}\nRequesting Notification of a channel reestablishment\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall call the\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocol-\nHandler::NotifyReestablishment\nmethod of a\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation, with the parameter\nchannelId\nset to the identifier of the\nChannel\n,\nwhere it needs a re-establishment notification.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00357]\n{DRAFT}\nValidity/lifetime of a Notification Request\nd\nA notifica-\ntion request registered at a\nUDS Transport Protocol\nimplementation according to\n[SWS_DM_00356] is valid only for the next call to\nara::diag::uds_transport::\nUdsTransportProtocolHandler::Start\nuntil the following call to\nara::diag::\nuds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Stop\nof this\nUDS Trans-\nport Protocol\nimplementation.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00358]\n{DRAFT}\nNotification of a channel reestablishment\nd\nUDS\nTransport Protocol\nimplementation shall call\nara::diag::uds_transport::\nUdsTransportProtocolMgr::ChannelReestablished\non its\nUdsTransport-\nProtocolMgr\nreference ((see [SWS_DM_00330]) setting the\nglobalChannelId\nargument to the tuple consisting of its own\nhandlerIdent\nand the\nChannelID\nit\nhas received in\nNotifyReestablishment\n(see [SWS_DM_00356]) once, in case it\ndetects, that the underlying network\nChannel\nrepresented by\nChannelID\nis getting\navailable again.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n[SWS_DM_00359]\n{DRAFT}\nPersistent Storage of Notification Request\nd\nUDS\nTransport Protocol\nimplementation shall store the notification request (see\n[SWS_DM_00356]) persistently, to be able to fulfill the notification even after a\nDM\nrestart.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04168)\n81 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo do this the\nTransport Protocol Manager\nuses the following information as\nprovided by the\nTransport Protocol Handler\nindication function on received\nUDS requests:\n\u000f\nTarget Address\n\u000f\nTarget Address Type (phys / func)\nIn transmit direction the\nTransport Protocol Manager\nprovides the UDS mes-\nsage from the Diagnostic Server and calls the Transmit method from the\nTransport\nProtocol Handler\n.\n[SWS_DM_00390]\n{DRAFT}\nDispatching physical Request\nd\nDM\nshall dispatch each\nUDS physical request to the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nresponsible for the\nSoftwareCluster\nwith\ndiagnosticAddress\nmatching the TargetAddress of the\nreceived UDS request and\naddressSemantics\nset to\nphysicalAddress\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04216)\n[SWS_DM_00391]\n{DRAFT}\nDispatching functional Request\nd\nDM\nshall dispatch\neach UDS functional request to all\nDiagnostic Server instances\nresponsible for\nthose\nSoftwareCluster\ns with a\ndiagnosticAddress\nmatching the TargetAddress\nof the received UDS request and\naddressSemantics\nset to\nfunctionalAddress\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04216)\n7.3\nSOVD\nTransport Layer\nBeside the opportunity to perform diagnostic communication between a\ndiagnostic\nclient\nand the Diagnostic Manager via\nDoIP\n, the\nDM\nwill provide further communi-\ncation interfaces for\nSOVD\n-based communication. This needs to be checked in the constructor.\n7.4.2 Diagnostic Communication Management\nA central element in the handling of diagnostic communication is the term\nDiagnos-\ntic Conversation\n, which is described in section 7.4.2.1.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n(RS_Diag_04233)\n[SWS_DM_01224]\n{DRAFT}\nDiagnostic service dynamic access-rights verification\nd\nIf the check in [SWS_DM_01223] is unsuccessful, the\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall additionally check if the requested Diagnostic Service is allowed by the\nclient DynamicAccessList by applying a pattern match on the received\nUDS\nrequest\ntowards the DynamicAccessList elements. The check is considered as successful if\nall the bytes of one entry of the DynamicAccessList are matching the\nUDS\nrequest.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04233)\nFurther bytes in the\nUDS\nrequest are not relevant.\nExample 1:\nDynamicAccessList: 31 01 13F4\nAny Routine Control Service with StartRoutine 13F4 would be accepted, regardless of\nthe routineControlOptionRecords.\nExample 2:\nDynamicAccessList: 11\nAny ECUReset Service would be accepted, regardless of the subfunction.\n[SWS_DM_01225]\n{DRAFT}\nResponse behavior of services without access\nrights\nd\nIf the service execution verification fails due to a failed check in scope\nof [SWS_DM_01223] and [SWS_DM_01224], the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send a negative Response with\nNRC\n`0x34 (authenticationRequired)' and stop the\nservice processing.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04233)\n[SWS_DM_01772]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'authentication required'\nto IdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service request is not having\nthe required authentication, the\nDM\nshall report a security event\nSEV_UDS_REQUESTED_ACTIONS_REQUIRES_AUTHENTICATION to IdsM (see\n[11] and table [SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01931].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01931]\n{DRAFT}\nd"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.5 UDS request Validation/Verification\n[SWS_DM_00096]\n{DRAFT}\nValidation Steps and Order\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server\ninstance\nshall execute the request validation, negative response code determination\nand processing according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196, RS_Diag_04203)\nISO 14229-1[1] describes a common processing for all requests in Figure 5  General\nserver response behavior. There are further optional\nSID\nspecific processing se-\nquences. This document describes the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nbehavior\nfor certain types of checks:\n\u000f\nmanufacturer specific failure detected?\nDecision by applying manufacturer\nspecific checks according to section 7.4.2.5.4\n\u000f\nSID supported?\nDecision according to section 7.4.2.5.2\n\u000f\nSID supported in active session?\nDecision according to section 7.4.2.5.3\n\u000f\nSID security check o.k.?\nDecision according to section 7.4.2.5.3\n\u000f\nsupplier-specific failure detected?\nDecision by applying supplier-specific\nchecks according to section 7.4.2.5.4\n[SWS_DM_00097]\n{DRAFT}\nAbort on failed verification step\nd\nWhenever one of the\nverification steps fails, further processing of the request shall be aborted and a negative\nresponse shall be sent back.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\nThe negative response code to be used will be defined in each step described in the\nfollowing sections.\n7.4.2.5.1 UDS request format checks\n[SWS_DM_00098]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS message checks\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall check, whether the diagnostic request is syntactically correct. I.e.\nwhether it conforms to ISO 14229-1 message format specification. If it does not con-\nform, the Verification shall be considered as failed and the negative response code\nshall be 0x13 (\nincorrectMessageLengthOrInvalidFormat\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_01778]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'incorrect message length or in-\nvalid format' to IdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service request is not cor-\nrect in the length or the format, the\nDM\nshall report a security event\nSEV_UDS_INCORRECT_MESSAGE_LENGTH_OR_FORMAT to IdsM (see [11] and\ntable [SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01932].\nc\n(RS_Ids_-\n00810)\n[SWS_DM_01932]\n{DRAFT}\nd"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n()\n7.4.2.5.2 Supported service checks\n[SWS_DM_00099]\n{DRAFT}\nSupported Service SID level checks\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nshall check, whether there is a configured internal or external\nservice processor for the incoming diagnostic request. If there is no service processor\non\nSID\nlevel, the Verification shall be considered as failed and the negative response\ncode shall be 0x11 (\nserviceNotSupported\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_01780]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting service not supported to IdsM\nd\nshall report\na security event SEV_UDS_SERVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED to IdsM (see [11] and table\n[SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01933].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01933]\n{DRAFT}\nd"

      "source_page": 106,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.4: SEV on 'Service not supported'\nc\n()\n[SWS_DM_00100]\n{DRAFT}\nSupported Service subfunction level checks\nd\nThe\nDi-\nagnostic Server instance\nshall check, whether there is a configured internal or\nexternal service processor for the incoming diagnostic request. If there exists a service\nprocessor on\nSID\nlevel, but not for the subfunction of the request, the Verification shall\nbe considered as failed and the negative response code shall be 0x12 (\nsubFunc-\ntionNotSupported\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_01779]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'service subfunction not supported' to IdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service subfunction is not supported, the\nDM\nshall report a secu-\nrity event SEV_UDS_SUBFUNCTION_NOT_SUPPORTED to IdsM (see [11] and table\n[SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01934].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01934]\n{DRAFT}\nd"

If\nDiagnosticServiceInstance\nhas\nno access permissions in the current Diagnostic Session and:\n\u000f\neither the\nSID\nof the service has no subfunction\n\u000f\nor all other sub-functions also have no access permissions in the current Diag-\nnostic Session,\nthe Verification shall be considered as failed and the negative response code shall be\n0x7F (\nserviceNotSupportedInActiveSession\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203, RS_Diag_-\n04006)\n[SWS_DM_00102]\n{DRAFT}\nSession Access subfunction level Permission\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall check, whether the service processor (\nDi-\nagnosticServiceInstance\n), which is assigned to handle the service has the per-\nmission to process the service in the current Diagnostic Session according to its\nDiagnosticAccessPermission\n.\ndiagnosticSession\n. If\nDiagnosticServi-\nceInstance\nhas no access permissions in the current Diagnostic Session and:\n\u000f\nthe\nSID\nof the service has subfunctions\n\u000f\nand at least one other sub-functions has access permissions in the current Diag-\nnostic Session,\nthe Verification shall be considered as failed and the negative response code shall be\n0x7E (\nsubFunctionNotSupportedInActiveSession\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203, RS_-\nDiag_04006)\n[SWS_DM_00103]\n{DRAFT}\nSecurity Access level Permission\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nshall check, whether the service processor (\nDiagnosticServi-\nceInstance\n), which is assigned to handle the service has the permission to process\nthe service in the current Security-Level according to its\nDiagnosticAccessPer-\nmission\n.\nsecurityLevel\n. If\nDiagnosticServiceInstance\nhas no access per-\nmissions in the current Security-Level, the Verification shall be considered as failed\nand the negative response code shall be 0x33 (\nsecurityAccessDenied\n).\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04203, RS_Diag_04005)\n[SWS_DM_01777]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'security access denied' to IdsM\nd\nIn case\na diagnostic service request is not allowed in the current security level, the\nDM\nshall\nreport a security event SEV_UDS_SECURITY_ACCESS_DENIED to IdsM (see [11]\nand table [SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in the table x4.\nc\n(RS_Ids_-\n00810)"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nmission to process the service in the current Security Level according to its\nDiagnos-\nticAccessPermission\n.\nsecurityLevel\n. If\nDiagnosticServiceInstance\nhas\nno access permissions in the current Security Level and:\n\u000f\nthe\nSID\nof the service has subfunctions\n\u000f\nand at least one other sub-functions has access permissions in the current Se-\ncurity Level,\nthe Verification shall be considered as failed and the negative response code shall be\n0x33 (\nsecurityAccessDenied\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n7.4.2.5.4 Manufacturer and Supplier Permission Checks and Confirmation\nTo allow manufacturer specific\nUDS\nservice pre-processing or filtering, ISO 14229-1[1]\ndefines manufacturer and supplier specific callouts. There are various use cases for\nthese callouts, among them are:\n\u000f\nUDS\nmessage filtering\n\u000f\nAdding project or customer specific diagnostic service processing\nUDS\nand the\nDM\nallows multiple of these callouts and the result of each of the callout\ncan be one of:\n\u000f\nContinue to process the service by the\nDM\n\u000f\nDiscarding the received diagnostic message without further response\n\u000f\nForcing a certain\nNRC\nto be send\nBoth, manufacturer and suppliers specific service callouts, are realized by\nara::\ndiag::ServiceValidation::Validate\naccording to its modeled instance given\nby [TPS_MANI_01352] and [constr_10063].\n[SWS_DM_01252]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of manufacturer service validations\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support manufacturer specific service validation checks according to ISO 14229-\n1[1] by calling\nara::diag::ServiceValidation::Validate\nfor each configured\nmanufacturer service check.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n[SWS_DM_01253]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of supplier service validations\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall\nsupport supplier specific service validation checks according to ISO 14229-1[1] by call-\ning\nara::diag::ServiceValidation::Validate\nfor each configured supplier\nservice check.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n[SWS_DM_01254]\n{DRAFT}\nContinue service processing after validation\nd\nIf a call\nto\nara::diag::ServiceValidation::Validate\nreturns without an error, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall continue to process the service according to\nISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n108 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "source_page": 109,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01255]\n{DRAFT}\nNRC\nafter failed service validation\nd\nIf a call to\nara::\ndiag::ServiceValidation::Validate\nreturns any error code except\nkNoPro-\ncessingNoResponse\n, the validation is be considered as failed and a negative re-\nsponse code equal to the value of the error code according to [SWS_DM_00547] shall\nbe sent as response.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n[SWS_DM_00859]\n{DRAFT}\nConfirmation of service processing\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nshall call the method\nara::diag::ServiceValidation::\nConfirmation\non every service instances for which\nara::diag::ServiceVal-\nidation::Validate\nwas called. If message handling results in sending a pos-\nitive or negative response, the\nara::diag::ServiceValidation::Confirma-\ntion\ncall shall be deferred after reception of\nara::diag::uds_transport::Ud-\nsTransportProtocolMgr::TransmitConfirmation\n. In any other case, it shall\nbe the last step of request processing.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04019, RS_Diag_04172)\n[SWS_DM_00860]\n{DRAFT}\nNo service processing\nd\nIf any\nara::diag::Service-\nValidation::Validate\nreturns\nkNoProcessingNoResponse\n, the\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nshall discard the message of received diagnostic request.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04196, RS_Diag_04199)\n7.4.2.5.5 Condition checks\nIn some cases, diagnostic functionality shall only be executed if the vehicle is in a\ncertain state. An example is the condition that the vehicle is stopped (vehicle speed\nequals 0).\n[SWS_DM_00111]\n{DRAFT}\nConfigurable environment condition checks\nd\nThe\nDi-\nagnostic Server instance\nshall perform a condition check when the ISO 14229-\n1[1] mentions a service specific \"Condition check\" in the defined\nNRC\nhandling for a\ngiven diagnostic service. The\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send the con-\nfigured\nNRC\nvalue (see [SWS_DM_00289]) if the condition is not fulfilled.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04199)\n[SWS_DM_00112]\n{DRAFT}\nCondition check definition\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server\ninstance\nshall execute a condition check according to [SWS_DM_00111] by the pres-\nence of a\nDiagnosticEnvironmentalCondition\nreferenced in the role\nenviron-\nmentalCondition\nby the processed\nDiagnosticServiceInstance\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04199)\n[SWS_DM_00286]\n{DRAFT}\nConfigurable environmental condition check execu-\ntion\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall execute an environmental condi-\ntion check before executing the requested service if defined. (see\nDiagnosticEnvi-\nronmentalCondition\nelement from DEXT [3]).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n[SWS_DM_00287]\n{DRAFT}\nConfigurable environmental condition check criteria\nd\nThe environmental condition check shall be done by evaluation of the configured\nDiagnosticEnvConditionFormula\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n109 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },

      "source_page": 110,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nDiagnosticEnvConditionFormula\nmay reference a\nDiagnosticDataEle-\nment\nby a\nDiagnosticEnvDataCondition\nwith a logical operator given as\nDiag-\nnosticEnvCompareCondition\n.\n[SWS_DM_00288]\n{DRAFT}\nConfigurable environmental condition check evalu-\nates to\nTRUE\nd\nIf the computation of the\nDiagnosticEnvConditionFormula\nevalu-\nated to\nTRUE\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall execute the requested ser-\nvice.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n[SWS_DM_00970]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior of failed data element retrieval\nd\nIf the retrieval\nof the\ndataElement\nfailed due to an external processor has an error of\nara::diag::\nDiagUdsNrcErrorDomain\n, the\nDM\nshall treat the\nDiagnosticEnvConditionFor-\nmulaPart\nas condition not fulfilled and trigger a Log and Trace message.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04199)\n[SWS_DM_00289]\n{DRAFT}\nConfigurable environmental condition check evalu-\nates to\nFALSE\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send the\nNRC\ndefined in\nnrcValue\n, if the computation of the\nDiagnosticEnvConditionFormula\nevaluated\nto\nFALSE\n. If\nnrcValue\ndoes not define a\nNRC\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send NRC 0x22 (\nConditionsNotCorrect\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04199)\n7.4.2.6 UDS response handling\n[SWS_DM_01258]\n{DRAFT}\nResponse handling\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall process diagnostic responses according to ISO 14229-1[1]. This in-\ncludes sending of positive and negative responses, as well as suppression of negative\nor positive responses.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196, RS_Diag_04020)\n[SWS_DM_00368]\n{DRAFT}\nDM\ntakes care of Response Pending Messages\nd\nIf the\nprocessing of a diagnostic service requires more time than allowed by the P2/P2* timer\nof the current session, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send a negative\nresponse with NRC 0x78 (requestCorrectlyReceivedResponsePending) according to\nISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04016)\n[SWS_DM_00369]\n{DRAFT}\nMaximum number of busy responses\nd\nIf the num-\nber of negative responses for a requested diagnostic request reaches the value de-\nfined in the configuration parameter\nmaxNumberOfRequestCorrectlyReceive-\ndResponsePending\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nmodule shall cancel the\nprocessing of the active diagnostic internal or external request processing, according to\n[SWS_DM_00277], [SWS_DM_00278] and send a negative response with NRC 0x10\n(\ngeneralReject\n).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04016)\n[SWS_DM_01257]\n{DRAFT}\nResourceTemporarilyNotAvailable NRC handling\nd\nIf\nthe\nDM\nis processing a diagnostic service using a ara::diag interface different than\nara::diag::ServiceValidation\n, that requires the offer(), and if this interface is\nnot offered yet or not offered any more, the\nDM\nshall return an\nNRC\n0x94 (ResourceTem-\nporarilyNotAvailable).\nc\n()\n110 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.7 Keep track of active non-default sessions\n[SWS_DM_00380]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport for S3 timer\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall provide support for S3\nServer\n(session timeout) with a server specific value\naccording to [SWS_DM_01747]. The timer handling shall be implemented according\nto ISO 14229-2[12].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04006)\n[SWS_DM_01747]\n{DRAFT}\nS3 timer value\nd\nIf the parameter\nDiagnosticSession-\nControlClass\n.\ns3ServerTimeout\nis not configured, the\nDiagnostic Server\ninstance\n(Software Cluster), shall take the value of 5000ms as the S3Server time-\nout. If the parameter\nDiagnosticSessionControlClass\n.\ns3ServerTimeout\nis\nconfigured, the Diagnostic Server Instance (Software Cluster) shall take the configured\nvalue as the S3Server timeout.\nc\n()\n[SWS_DM_00381]\n{DRAFT}\nSession timeout\nd\nWhenever a non-default session is ac-\ntive and when the session timeout (S3\nServer\n) is reached without receiving any diagnostic\nrequest, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall reset to the default session state.\nDiagnostic Server instance\ninternal states for service processing shall be reset\naccording to ISO 14229-2[12].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04006)\n[SWS_DM_00382]\n{DRAFT}\nSession timeout start\nd\nThe session timeout timer\n(S3\nserver\n) shall be started on\n\u000f\nCompletion of any final response message or an error indication during sending\nof the response ([SWS_DM_00312])\n\u000f\nCompletion of the requested action in case no response message (positive and\nnegative) is required / allowed.\n\u000f\nIn case of an error during the reception of a multi-frame request message\n([SWS_DM_00310])\nStart of S3\nServer\nmeans reset the timer and start counting from the beginning.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04006)\n[SWS_DM_00383]\n{DRAFT}\nSession timeout stop\nd\nThe session timeout timer\n(S3\nServer\n) shall be stopped when the reception of an\nUDS\nmessage was indicated\n([SWS_DM_00309]).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04006)\n[SWS_DM_00812]\n{DRAFT}\nRe-enabling on transition to default session\nd\nIf\nDTC\nsetting is disabled and\nDM\nis transitioning into default session, then\nDM\nshall enable the\nDTC\nsetting again.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04006)\n7.4.2.8 UDS service processing\nThis chapter describes the\nUDS\nservice processing behavior of the\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\n.\n[SWS_DM_00127]\n{DRAFT}\nAvailability of diagnostic service processors\nd\nThe\nDi-\nagnostic Server instance\nshall provide a service processor on SID level for all\n111 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P113_152",
      "source_element": "SWS_DM_00129",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 113,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nMemory related\nUDS\nservices (such as 0x34 RequestDownload) use the request pa-\nrameter addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier to identify the number of bytes transmitted\non the bus for memory address and size. Regardless of the wire representation of\naddress and length information, within the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nand ex-\nternal service processors all addresses and data length information are mapped to a\nuint64 datatype.\n[SWS_DM_00129]\n{DRAFT}\nSupported addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall support for each nibble of the addressAn-\ndLengthFormatIdentifier a value between 1 and 8.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04120)\n[SWS_DM_00130]\n{DRAFT}\nNot supported addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send the negative response 0x31 (re-\nquestOutOfRange), if an addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier with a value outside the\nrange between 1 and 8 is received.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04120)\n[SWS_DM_01762]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'Sequence error' to IdsM\nd\nIn case\na diagnostic service is received, which results in a negative response with\nNRC 0x24 (requestSequenceError)\n, the\nDM\nshall report a security event\nSEV_UDS_REQUEST_SEQUENCE_ERROR (see [11] and table [SWS_DM_01760])\nwith the context data given in [SWS_DM_01935].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01935]\n{DRAFT}\nd"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nconfiguration contains a\nDiagnosticReadDTCInformation\nof\ncategory\n'RE-\nPORT_USER_DEF_MEMORY_DTC_SNAPSHOT_RECORD_BY_DTC_NUMBER'.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04180, RS_Diag_04157, RS_Diag_04067)\n7.4.2.8.7.11 SF 0x19  reportUserDefMemoryDTCExtDataRecordByDTCNumber\n[SWS_DM_00374]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of\nUDS\nservice ReadDTCInformation,\nSubfunction 0x19\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall support Sub-\nfunction 0x19 (reportUserDefMemoryDTCExtDataRecordByDTCNumber) of the\nUDS\nservice 0x19 ReadDTCInformation according to ISO 14229-1[1], provided the\nconfiguration contains a\nDiagnosticReadDTCInformation\nof\ncategory\n'RE-\nPORT_USER_DEF_MEMORY_DTC_EXT_DATA_RECORD_BY_DTC_NUMBER'.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04180, RS_Diag_04157, RS_Diag_04067)\n7.4.2.8.8 Service 0x22  ReadDataByIdentifier\nThe processing of a\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22) is described in ISO\n14229-1[1], see in particular the evaluation sequence in Figure 15. On processing,\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nneeds to perform various checks. The follow-\ning requirements determine the relation between the input data to be checked and the\nconfiguration provided to the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nvia\nDEXT\nparameters.\n[SWS_DM_00170]\n{DRAFT}\nRealisation of\nUDS\nservice ReadDataByIdentifier\n(0x22)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the diagnostic ser-\nvice 0x22 ReadDataByIdentifier according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_00412]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck requested number of DataIdentifiers\nd\nOn recep-\ntion of the\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), the\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall check the number of the requested DataIdentifiers within one message.\nIn case a\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22) request contains more DataIdenti-\nfiers than defined by\nmaxDidToRead\n, the request shall be rejected with\nNRC\n(0x13).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_00409]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier\nd\nOn reception of the\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), a requested DataIdentifier shall be consid-\nered as supported if and only if there exists a\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nwith\nid\nmatching the DataIdentifier and this\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nis referenced by\na\nDiagnosticReadDataByIdentifier\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_00413]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier in active session\nd\nOn\nreception of the\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), a requested DataIdenti-\nfier shall be considered as supported in active session if and only if the DataIdentifier\nis supported according to [SWS_DM_00409] and the\nDiagnosticDataByIdenti-\nfier\n.\naccessPermission\nreferences by its\nDiagnosticAccessPermission\n.\ndi-\nagnosticSession\nthe active diagnostic session in the\nDM\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n124 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00414]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier on active security\nlevel\nd\nOn reception of the\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), a requested\nDataIdentifier shall be considered as supported on active security level if and only if\nthe DataIdentifier is supported according to [SWS_DM_00409] and the\nDiagnos-\nticDataByIdentifier\n.\naccessPermission\nreferences by its\nDiagnosticAc-\ncessPermission\n.\nsecurityLevel\nthe active security level in the\nDM\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04203)\n[SWS_DM_00570]\n{DRAFT}\nRetrieving data for requested DataIdentifier\nd\nOn re-\nception of the\nUDS\nService ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), the\nDiagnostic Server\ninstance\nshall retrieve the mapped data for that DataIdentifier.\nThere are various ways how DID data retrieving is modeled. Among them are:\n\u000f\nreceived entire DID via ara::diag interface [SWS_DM_00601] or\n[SWS_DM_00607]\n\u000f\nreceived data for data elements via ara::diag interface [SWS_DM_00603]\n\u000f\ngeneric\nUDS\nservice processing [SWS_DM_00602]\n\u000f\ninternal data [SWS_DM_00393]\nc\n(RS_Diag_04097)\nNote: Also, a\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\n's single\ndataElement\n(referenced by\na meta-class\nDiagnosticDataElement\n) can be accessed from the associated\nRPortPrototype\n. Whether a security level is applicable by the\nDiagnostic-\nSecurityAccess\nis defined by\nsecurityLevel\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04208)\n[SWS_DM_01776]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'security unlocked successfully for security\naccess' to IdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service\nSecurityAccess\nwith subfunction\nCompareKey\nis received, which successfully unlocks the requested security access\ntype, the\nDM\nshall report a security event SEV_UDS_ECU_UNLOCK_SUCCESSFUL\nto IdsM (see [11] and table [SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in\n[SWS_DM_01939].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01939]\n{DRAFT}\nd"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00270]\n{DRAFT}\nCounting of attempts to change security level\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall count the number of failed attempts to\nchange a requested security level. The Counter shall be reset if the security level\nchange has passed successfully.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04005)\n[SWS_DM_00271]\n{DRAFT}\nEvaluate the number of failed security level change\nattempts\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall compare the number of failed\nDiagnosticSecurityLevel\nchanges with threshold value\nnumFailedSecurity-\nAccess\nafter each failed attempt.\nIf the number of failed attempts is below the threshold value\nnumFailedSecurity-\nAccess\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall send a negative response with\nNRC\n0x35 (InvalidKey).\nIf the number of failed attempts reaches the threshold value\nnumFailedSecurityAc-\ncess\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall start a delay timer configured with\nvalue\nsecurityDelayTime\n(see [SWS_DM_00272]) and send a negative response\nwith\nNRC\n0x36 (exceededNumberOfAttempts).\nIn both cases a\nDiagnosticSecurityLevel\nchange must not be done if the attempt\nfailed before.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04005)\nThe delay timer represents the required minimum time between security access at-\ntempts, after one time negative response with\nNRC\n0x36 (exceededNumberOfAttempts)\nwas sent out.\n[SWS_DM_01775]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'security access with invalid key' to\nIdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service\nSecurityAccess\nwith subfunction\nCom-\npareKey\nis received, which is failing and the maximum number of al-\nlowed failed attempts not yet reached, the\nDM\nshall report a security event\nSEV_UDS_SECURITY_ACCESS_INVALID_KEY to IdsM (see [11] and table\n[SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01940].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_DM_01940]\n{DRAFT}\nd"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00480]\n{DRAFT}\nShared Security Access Delay Timer\nd\nIf\nDiagnostic-\nSecurityAccessClass\n.\nsharedTimer\nis set to true, a shared delay timer instance\nshall be used for all security levels.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04005)\nThe effect of a started security access delay timer is always according to\n[SWS_DM_00272].\n7.4.2.8.10 Service 0x28  CommunicationControl\n[SWS_DM_00140]\n{DRAFT}\nRealisation of\nUDS\nservice 0x28 CommunicationCon-\ntrol\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the diagnostic service\n0x28 CommunicationControl according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_00252]\n{DRAFT}\nReaction on Unsupported Subfunction\nd\nThe\nDiag-\nnostic Server instance\nshall check, whether the Subfunction addressed by the\nCommunicationControl is supported by an existing\nDiagnosticComControl\n.\ncate-\ngory\nin the configuration and allow further processing.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01056]\n{DRAFT}\nOptional condition checks for sending periodic\nDIDs\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticDynamicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\ncheckPer-\nSourceId\nis set to TRUE, the\nDM\nshall transmit the\nPDID\nonly if the session, security\nand mode checks were executed successfully.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\n[SWS_DM_01057]\n{DRAFT}\nOptional stopping\nPDIDs\nafter session change\nd\nIf\nDi-\nagnosticDynamicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\ncheckPerSourceId\nis\nset to TRUE and the\nDM\nis changing the diagnostic session, the\nDM\nshall remove all\nPDIDs\nfrom the list of scheduled\nPDIDs\nthat are not allowed to be read in the new\nsession.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\n[SWS_DM_01058]\n{DRAFT}\nOptional stopping\nPDIDs\nafter security level\nchange\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticDynamicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\ncheck-\nPerSourceId\nis set to TRUE and the\nDM\nis changing the security level session, the\nDM\nshall remove all\nPDIDs\nfrom the list of scheduled\nPDIDs\nthat are not allowed to be\nread in the new security level.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\n[SWS_DM_01059]\n{DRAFT}\nNo periodic\nDIDs\nin default session\nd\nWhen the diag-\nnostic session changes to or is in the DefaultSession, the\nDM\nshall stop all scheduled\nperiodic\nDIDs\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\nScheduler Periodic Transmission\nISO 14229-1[1] defines two distinct scheduler types for ReadDataByPeriodicIdenti-\nfier. The\nDM\nuses only scheduler type 1 as transmission strategy and NumPeri-\nodicAddr is identical to\nDiagnosticReadDataByPeriodicIDClass\n.\nscheduler-\nMaxNumber\n. This means that with each scheduler call, all the configured\nPDIDs\nfor\nthat scheduler rate are transmitted.\n[SWS_DM_01060]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of Scheduler type 1\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support the\nscheduling of\nPDIDs\nbased on scheduler type 1 as defined in ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04215)\n[SWS_DM_01061]\n{DRAFT}\nTrigger all scheduled\nPDIDs\nper scheduler\nd\nWhen a\nperiodic scheduler elapses for a requested transmission rate, the\nDM\nshall trigger the\ntransmission of all scheduled\nPDIDs\nassigned to this transmission rate.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04215)\n[SWS_DM_01062]\n{DRAFT}\nTransmission of all\nPDIDs\non the periodic connection\nd\nIf the\nPDID\ntransmission is triggered for a requested transmission rate, the\nDM\nshall\ntransmit all\nPDIDs\non the periodic transmission on the periodic connection starting with\nthe first\nPDID\nin the list of scheduled\nPDIDs\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\n[SWS_DM_01063]\n{DRAFT}\nTransmission error behavior\nd\nIn case of a\nPDID\ntrans-\nmission error, the\nDM\nshall use always the same order of periodicDIDs per client. Trans-\nmission errors shall not influence this order, the\nDM\nshall continue to retry the trans-\nmission and start the next\nPDID\nonly after the\nPDID\nwas transmitted successfully.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04215)\n138 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.8.13 Service 0x2C  DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier\n[SWS_DM_01070]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of\nUDS\nservice 0x2C in Adaptive AUTOSAR\nDM\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the diagnostic service\n0x2C DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier with subfunctions 0x01 (defineByIdentifier) and\n0x03 (clearDynamicallyDefinedDataIdentifier) according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04246)\nThe support of subfunction 0x02 (defineByMemoryAddress) is not appropriate in an\nAUTOSAR Adaptive system. These systems have mostly more virtual address spaces.\nTherefore, this subfunction is not supported.\nAll testers share the same\nDDDID\n. In default session the last defined\nDDDID\nwill be\nused. The client can switch to a non-default session ensure that no other testers\ninterfere with it's\nDDDIDs\n.\n[SWS_DM_01071]\n{DRAFT}\nNo persistency of defined\nDDDIDs\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticDy-\nnamicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\nconfigurationHandling\nis set to\nvolatile, the\nDM\nshall initialize all\nDDDIDs\nas not present at\nDM\nInitialization.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04246)\n[SWS_DM_01072]\n{DRAFT}\nPersistency of defined\nDDDIDs\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticDynam-\nicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\nconfigurationHandling\nis set to non-\nVolatile, the\nDM\nshall persist\nDDDIDs\nconfigured by the\nUDS\nservice 0x2C and restore\nthe\nDDDIDs\ndefinition from Non-Volatile Memory at\nDM\nInitialization.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04246)\n[SWS_DM_01073]\n{DRAFT}\nDM behavior for subfunction 'defineByIdentifier'\nd\nOn\nreception of service 'DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier' with subfunction size.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04246)\n[SWS_DM_01074]\n{DRAFT}\nOnly static\nDIDs\nas sourceDataIdentifier\nd\nIf the\nDM\nis\nreceiving the service 'DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier' with subfunction 'defineByIden-\ntifier' and one or more of the sourceDataIdentifier are itself a active dynamically defined\ndata identifier, the\nDM\nshall return an\nNRC\n0x31 (requestOutOfRange).\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04246)\n[SWS_DM_01075]\n{DRAFT}\nMaximum number of sourceDataIdentifiers in the re-\nquest\nd\nIf the\nDM\nreceives the\nUDS\nservice If\nthe\nDDDID\ncannot be defined in the current session, the\nDM\nshall return an\nNRC\n0x31\n(requestOutOfRange).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04246)\n[SWS_DM_01080]\n{DRAFT}\nSecurity level check for\nDDDID\nd\nOn reception of\nservice 'DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier' with subfunction 'defineByIdentifier', the\nDM\nshall check if the\nDDDIDs\ncan be defined in the security level according to\n[SWS_DM_00414]. If the\nDDDID\ncannot be defined in the current security level, the\nDM\nshall return an\nNRC\n0x31 (requestOutOfRange).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04246)\n[SWS_DM_01081]\n{DRAFT}\nSession check for sourceDataIdentifier\nd\nOn recep-\ntion of service 'DynamicallyDefineDataIdentifier' with subfunction defineByIdenti-\nfier and if\nDiagnosticDynamicallyDefineDataIdentifierClass\n.\ncheckPer-\nSourceId\nis set to true, the\nDM\nshall check if the sourceDataIdentifier can be defined\nin the current session according to [SWS_DM_00413].       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.8.14 Service 0x2E  WriteDataByIdentifier\nThe processing of a\nUDS\nService WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E) is described in ISO\n14229-1[1], see in particular the evaluation sequence in Figure 21. On processing, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nneeds to perform various checks. The following\nrequirements determine the relation between the input data to be checked and the\nconfiguration provided to the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nvia\nDEXT\nparameters.\n[SWS_DM_00186]\n{DRAFT}\nRealisation of\nUDS\nservice WriteDataByIdentifier\n(0x2E)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the diagnostic ser-\nvice 0x2E WriteDataByIdentifier according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_00415]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier\nd\nOn reception of the\nUDS\nService WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E), a requested DataIdentifier shall be consid-\nered as supported if and only if there exists a\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nwith\nid\nmatching the DataIdentifier and this\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nis referenced by\na\nDiagnosticWriteDataByIdentifier\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_00416]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier in active session\nd\nOn\nreception of the\nUDS\nService WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E), a requested DataIdentifier\nshall be considered as supported in active session if and only if the DataIdentifier is\nsupported according to [SWS_DM_00415] and the active session passes the execution\npermission check as per [SWS_DM_00101].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04203)\n[SWS_DM_00417]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck supported DataIdentifier on active security\nlevel\nd\nOn reception of the\nUDS\nService WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E), a requested\nDataIdentifier shall be considered as supported on active security level if and only if\nthe DataIdentifier is supported according to [SWS_DM_00415] and the active security\nlevel passes the execution permission check as per [SWS_DM_00103].\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04203)\n[SWS_DM_00572]\n{DRAFT}\nWriting data for requested DataIdentifier\nd\nOn recep-\ntion of the\nUDS\nService WriteDataByIdentifier (0x2E) the\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall provide the data for a DataIdentifier to the mapped\nRPortPrototype\ns.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04097)\n[SWS_DM_00573]\n{DRAFT}\nReaction on ApplicationError\nd\nIf the\nara::core::Result\nof external processor has an error of\nara::diag::DiagUdsNrcErrorDomain\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall return a negative response with the value of\nthat error code.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_01764]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting 'Writing invalid data is requested' to IdsM\nd\nIn case a diagnostic service\nWriteDataByIdentifier\nis received, which results\nin a negative response with\nNRC 0x31 (requestOutOfRange)\n, the\nDM\nshall re-\nport a security event SEV_UDS_WRITE_INVALID_DATA to IdsM (see [11] and table\n[SWS_DM_01760]) with the context data given in [SWS_DM_01946].\nc\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n141 of 787 Document       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.8.18 Service 0x36  TransferData\n[SWS_DM_00137]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of\nUDS\nservice TransferData (0x36)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the\nUDS\nservice TransferData\n(0x36) according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_00869]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS service TransferData (0x36) download process-\ning\nd\nTo download data via the\nUDS\nservice TransferData, the\nDiagnostic Server\ninstance\nshall call\nara::diag::DownloadService::DownloadData\nto process\nthe service.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04033)\nISO 14229-1[1] provides a\nUDS\nservice TransferData (0x36) specific\nNRC\nevaluation\nsequence. This sequence has checks that in rotating order needs to be done by the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nand by the service processor itself. Therefore be-\nfore actually running the service processor, the service processor needs means to\ndo a certain verification step. As the GenericUDSService class has only one single\nmethod this is not possible for the GenericUDSService class. As a result of this, the\nentire service specific\nNRC\nhandling is inside the GenericUDSService class for\nUDS\nservice TransferData (0x36).\n[SWS_DM_01096]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS service TransferData (0x36) upload processing\nd\nTo upload data via the\nUDS\nservice TransferData, the\nDiagnostic Server in-\nstance\nshall call\nara::diag::UploadService::UploadData\nto process the ser-\nvice.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04033)\nBesides the\nNRC\nchecking according to [SWS_DM_00101] and [SWS_DM_00103] the\nDM\ndoes not further service validation. All other\nNRC\nchecks required by ISO 14229-\n1[1] for\nUDS\nservice TransferData have to be implemented in the application called in\n[SWS_DM_00869] and [SWS_DM_01096].\n7.4.2.8.19 Service 0x37  RequestTransferExit\n[SWS_DM_00141]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of\nUDS\nservice RequestTransferExit (0x37)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the\nUDS\nservice Request-\nTransferExit (0x37) according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n[SWS_DM_00871]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS service RequestTransferExit (0x37) download\nprocessing\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::Down-\nloadService::RequestDownloadExit\nto process a\nUDS\nservice RequestTrans-\nferExit (0x37) for a download.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04033)\n[SWS_DM_01097]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS service RequestTransferExit (0x37) upload pro-\ncessing\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::Upload-\nService::RequestUploadExit\nto process a\nUDS\nservice RequestTransferExit\n(0x37) for an upload.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04033)\n145 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nBesides the\nNRC\nchecking according to [SWS_DM_00101] and [SWS_DM_00103] the\nDM\ndoes not further service validation. All other\nNRC\nchecks required by ISO 14229-\n1[1] for UDS service TransferExit have to be implemented in the application called in\n[SWS_DM_00871] and [SWS_DM_01097].\n7.4.2.8.20 Service 0x38  RequestFileTransfer\nThis chapter describes the definition and use of the\nUDS\nservice RequestFileTransfer.\nThe API design had the goal to allow a maximum level of flexibility to efficiently ex-\nchange data or even very large data over process bounds in an AUTOSAR Adaptive\nsystem. An application developer of the\nara::diag::FileTransferService\nin-\nterface can choose between various ways to transfer the data. Some possible ways to\ndo so are:\n\u000f\nSimple: Copy the data between the adaptive application and the Diagnostic Man-\nagement. This approach scales well enough for smaller file sizes and the imple-\nmentation is simple.\n\u000f\nZero Copy: The data is not copied between the adaptive application and the\nDiagnostic Management. This approach is resources efficient and has a good\nruntime behavior, especially for larger data transfers.\n\u000f\nOS File System Handle: No data needs to be copied between the adaptive ap-\nplication and the Diagnostic Management. The application provides a file handle\nthat is used in scope of another process. Data is not copied, but stronger depen-\ndencies on the OS exist.\nIn general, the design is open to implement further strategies that meet the individual\nproject requirements.\n[SWS_DM_01310]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of UDS service RequestFileTransfer (0x38)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall implement the\nUDS\nservice Request-\nFileTransfer (0x38) according to ISO 14229-1[1]. Besides the\nNRC\nchecking according\nto [SWS_DM_00101] and [SWS_DM_00103] the\nDM\ndoes no further service validation.\nAll other\nNRC\nchecks required by ISO 14229-1[1] for\nUDS\nservice RequestFileTransfer\nhave to be implemented in the adaptive application.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01311]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation AddFile (0x01)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to AddFile (0x01) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::RequestWriteFile\nwith WriteFileMode equal to kAdd.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04135)\n[SWS_DM_01312]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation DeleteFile (0x02)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to DeleteFile (0x02) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::DeleteFile\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n146 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01313]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation ReplaceFile (0x03)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to ReplaceFile (0x03) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::RequestWriteFile\nwith WriteFileMode equal to kReplace.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01314]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation ReadFile (0x04)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to ReadFile (0x04) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::RequestReadFile\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01315]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation ReadDir (0x05)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to ReadDir (0x05) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::RequestReadDirectory\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01316]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of modeOfOperation ResumeFile (0x06)\nd\nIf\na service RequestFileTransfer with modeOfOperation equal to ResumeFile (0x06) is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::FileTrans-\nferService::RequestResumeWriteFile\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\nThe\nara::diag::FileTransferService\nmethods to process a RequestFileTrans-\nfer (0x38) all return a DataTransferReadSession or DataTransferWriteSession object.\nThis object is the connection of processing the RequestFileTransfer (0x38) and the\nconsecutive following TransferData (0x36) services. The 0x36 service that is used to\nactually transfer the files data stream is done within the\nara::diag::DataTrans-\nferReadSession\nor\nara::diag::DataTransferWriteSession\n. Within these\nobjects various overloaded template constructors exist, that allow that the actual im-\nplementation can be inside the handler objects that are part of these template con-\nstructors. This allows any custom implementation with different levels of optimization\nadapted for what is required by the ECU project.\nThe connection between RequestFileTransfer (0x38) and TransferData (0x36) is done\nusing the corresponding DataTransferReadSession or DataTransferWriteSession pro-\nvided by a successful processing of the RequestFileTransfer in the\nara::diag::\nFileTransferService\n. This data transfer session is used to abstract between the\nindividual selected strategies to handle the TransferData (0x36) data exchange be-\ntween the\nUDS\nprotocol and the final destination of the data. This design allows various\nhandler objects to be used. AUTOSAR provides a set of handlers to be choose by the\napplication developer that fits best to the induvial needs (e.g. shared memory or not).\nThe design is also open to provide further handler implementation in future AUTOSAR\nreleases as well as platform vendor specific extensions by adding further template\nconstructors for these handlers in the session objects.\n[SWS_DM_01317]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of TransferData (0x36) in context of Re-\nquestFileTransfer\nd\nIf a TransferData (0x36) in context of RequestFileTransfer is re-\nceived, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call (depending on the data di-\nrection read/write) the corresponding Read or Write methods of the handler classes\n147 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nregistered via the template constructors of DataTransferReadSession or DataTransfer-\nWriteSession.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01318]\n{DRAFT}\nRealization of RequestTransferExit (0x37) in context\nof RequestFileTransfer\nd\nIf a RequestTransferExit (0x37) in context of RequestFile-\nTransfer is received, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call (depending on\nthe data direction read/write) the Exit method of the handler classes registered via\nthe template constructors of DataTransferReadSession or DataTransferWriteSession.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n[SWS_DM_01319]\n{DRAFT}\nConsecutive registration of notifier with Release-\nHandler::SetNotifier()\nd\nIn case of a consecutive call of\nara::diag::Release-\nHandler::SetNotifier\nof the corresponding\nara::diag::ReleaseHandler\nin-\nstance, the\nDM\nshall overwrite the previous registered notifier.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04135)\nSecurity and Rights Management\nUDS\nand\nDEXT\nallow only a very coarse use of the DiagnosticAccessPermission on\nservice RequestFileTransfer level. A DiagnosticAccessPermission on file level would\nrequire a static definition of filenames in\nDEXT\n, which is against the nature of a generic\nfile system. This is a difference to the handling of DIDs or RIDs that are defined in\nDEXT\n.\nAs further level a filesystem has a rights management implemented inside the OS and\ntherefore outside the scope of the\nDiagnostic Server instance\n. This means\nthat rights management for file access needs to be done in scope of the adaptive\napplication implementing the\nara::diag::FileTransferService\n.\n7.4.2.8.21 Service 0x3E  TesterPresent\n[SWS_DM_00126]\n{DRAFT}\nRealisation of\nUDS\nservice 0x3E TesterPresent\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall internally implement the diagnostic service\n0x3E TesterPresent according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04196)\n7.4.2.8.22 Service 0x85  ControlDTCSetting\nThe\nUDS\nservice ControlDTCSetting is used by a client to stop or resume the updating\nof DTC status bits in the server.\n[SWS_DM_00229]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport of\nUDS\nservice ControlDTCSetting (0x85)\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall provide the\nUDS\nservice ControlDTCSetting\n(0x85) according to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04180, RS_Diag_04159)\n[SWS_DM_00444]\n{DRAFT}\nCheck Support of\nUDS\nservice ControlDTCSetting\n(0x85) in active session\nd\nOn reception of the\nUDS\nservice ControlDTCSetting (0x85),\na requested subfunction shall be considered as supported in active session if and only\n148 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.22: SEV on 'DTC setting switched off'\nc\n()\n[SWS_DM_00811]\n{DRAFT}\nRe-enabling of ControlDTCSetting by Diagnostic Ap-\nplication\nd\nIn case the DTCSetting is disabled and the Diagnostic Server receives a\ncall to\nara::diag::DTCInformation::EnableControlDtc\nfunction from the ap-\nplication the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall:\n\u000f\nenable the update of the\nUDS DTC status byte\n\u000f\nenable the storage in event memory\n\u000f\nupdate\nara::diag::ControlDtcStatusType\nto\nkDTCSettingOn\nc\n(RS_Diag_04159, RS_Diag_04211, RS_Diag_04067)\nHint: The monitoring application is responsible for the re-enabling of ControlDTCSet-\nting in case some conditions or states demands so.       "verbatim_text": "Table 7.23: Supported sub function of ResponseonEvent (0x86)\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nsupports one active ResponseOnEvent logic\nper session (the default session or a non-default session) as specified by [1].       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01262]\n{DRAFT}\nNo storage of RoE events\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticRespon-\nseOnEventClass\n.\nstoreEventEnabled\nis set to FALSE and a RoE service with the\nstoreState bit (Bit6) set to true is received, the\nDM\nshall deny the request according to\nISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04160)\n[SWS_DM_01263]\n{DRAFT}\nStorage of RoE events\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticResponseOn-\nEventClass\n.\nstoreEventEnabled\nis set to TRUE, the\nDM\nshall support the func-\ntionaltiy of the\nRoE\nservice with the storeState bit (Bit6) set to true according to ISO\n14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04160)\n7.4.2.8.24 Custom Diagnostic Services\nIn addition to supported\nUDS\ndiagnostic services, as shown in Table 7.7, an\nOEM\nor\nsystem supplier may have a need for a diagnostic service which is not the part of the\nservices standardized in ISO 14229-1[1].\n[SWS_DM_00502]\n{DRAFT}\nSupport for Custom Diagnostic Services\nd\nThe\nDiag-\nnostic Server instance\nshall provide a service processor on\nSID\nlevel for a cus-\ntom services request (defined by\nDiagnosticCustomServiceInstance\n), which is\nspecified by a system supplier.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04177)\n[SWS_DM_00983]\n{DRAFT}\nProcessing of Custom Diagnostic Services\nd\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall call\nara::diag::GenericUDSService::\nHandleMessage\nto process a custom\nUDS\nservice by the given\nSID\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04177)\nMeta-class\nDiagnosticCustomServiceInstance\ncan be used to define the in-\nstance of a Custom Service. Modeling of Custom Diagnostic Services is described\nin the TPS Manifest Specification [ [10]].\nNote:\nSID\nrange for custom service requests is defined in Table 2 of ISO 14229-1[1].\n7.4.2.9 Cancellation of a Diagnostic Conversation\nThe cancellation of\nDiagnostic Conversation\ns and external processors is imple-\nmented by a CancellationHandler instance.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00277]\n{DRAFT}\nCancellation of a Diagnostic Conversation in case of\nExternal Service Processing\nd\nOn Cancellation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\nin\ncase a diagnostic request is currently processed in context of this\nDiagnostic Con-\nversation\nby a service processor external to the\nDiagnostic Server instance\n,\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall notify this external service processor, that\nthe processing for this service shall be canceled according to [SWS_DM_00577].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04167)\n[SWS_DM_00278]\n{DRAFT}\nCancellation of a Diagnostic Conversation in case of\nInternal Processing\nd\nOn Cancellation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\nin case a\ndiagnostic request is currently processed in context of this protocol internally within\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall\nabort the started activity as far as possible.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04167)\n[SWS_DM_00279]\n{DRAFT}\nCancellation of a Diagnostic Conversation before Re-\nsponse Transmission\nd\nOn Cancellation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\nin case a\ndiagnostic request is currently processed in context of this protocol and response trans-\nmission has not yet been started, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall abort\nall service processing and skip sending any response, which implies\nnot\nto call\nara::\ndiag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::Transmit\nof the\nrespective UDS Transport Protocol Handler.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04167)\n[SWS_DM_00280]\n{DRAFT}\nCancellation of a Diagnostic Conversation at Re-\nsponse Transmission\nd\nOn Cancellation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\nin case a\ndiagnostic request is currently processed in context of this\nDiagnostic Conversa-\ntion\nand\nara::diag::uds_transport::UdsTransportProtocolHandler::\nTransmit\nof the UDS TransportLayer was already called, nothing has to be done by\nthe\nDiagnostic Server instance\n. This implies a sent out response.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04167)\n[SWS_DM_00847]\n{DRAFT}\nReinitialization of Service Instance on Cancellation of\na Diagnostic Conversation\nd\nOn Cancellation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\n, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nshall reset the values of the fields of the associated\nara::diag::Conversation\nclass Instance according to [SWS_DM_00843].\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04167)\n[SWS_DM_00577]\n{DRAFT}\nCanceling external service processors\nd\nOn Cancel-\nlation of a\nDiagnostic Conversation\nin case a diagnostic request is currently\nprocessed within an external service processor, the supporting\nara::diag::Can-\ncellationHandler\nshall trigger all notifiers registered via\nara::diag::Cancel-\nlationHandler::SetNotifier\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04167)\n[SWS_DM_00984]\n{DRAFT}\nReturn of cancellation status\nd\nA call to\nara::diag::\nCancellationHandler::IsCanceled\nshall return false if the corresponding\nDi-\nagnostic Conversation\nis not canceled within its current processing state. On\nCancellation of this\nDiagnostic Conversation ara::diag::Cancellation-\nHandler::IsCanceled\nshall return true until the\nara::diag::Cancellation-\nHandler\nis destructed.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04167)\n154 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.3.4.6 Logging\n[SWS_DM_01928]\n{DRAFT}\nSOVD\nmethod for logging\nd\nIf a\nDiagnosticSovd-\nMethod\nin context of a\nDiagnosticSovdLog\nis configured the corresponding\nMethod for Logging\nshall be supported as per\nASAM SOVD\n[2].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04267)\n7.4.3.5 Configurable\nAPIs\nThis section describes how the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nrealizes the con-\nfigurable\nSOVD APIs\nas specified in\nASAM SOVD\n[2]. Generally there are two different\napproaches that are used to realize these\nSOVD APIs\n.\nFor\nSOVD APIs\nthat have a matching\nUDS\nServices, the realizing ara::diag interfaces\nare used for both protocols. Therefore this section aims on describing how the ex-\nisting configuration patterns are interpreted to realize the corresponding\nSOVD APIs\n.\nFor example a DiagnosticDataIdentifier with Service ReadByIdentifier (0x22) as of ISO\n14229-1[1] is also available as\nSOVD data\nthat supports the\nSOVD Read Single\nData Value from an Entity API\n. This means that the underlying ara::diag in-\nterfaces will be used for both protocols. Thus the realizing application will only provide\none ara::diag interface, that realizes the\nUDS\nService ReadByIdentifier (0x22) as well as\nthe\nSOVD Read Single Data Value from an Entity API\n. The following\nSOVD\nmethods are realized by this pattern:\n\u000f\nSOVD\ndata\n\u000f\nSOVD\nconfiguration (parameter only)\n\u000f\nSOVD\nfaults\n\u000f\nSOVD\noperations\n\u000f\nPredefined\nSOVD\nmode for\nCommunicationControl\nand\nControlDTCSet-\nting\nUnique\nSOVD APIs\n, that have no matching\nUDS\nService, are relaized by explicit mod-\neling and by using dedicated ara::diag interfaces.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe communication between the ara::diag interface and the\nDM\nitself is temporar-\nily interrupted\nIf the application would need to handle these situations to react on the not available\nDM\n, they would get very complex. To avoid this and to ease the interaction between\napplication and\nDM\nfor these functions, the ara::diag methods where the application\ncalling the\nDM\noutside of service processing, the\nDM\ncaches the relevant information\nand forwards this data to the\nDM\ninstance once it is available. The application itself can\nsimply concentrate on its function. Examples where this is applied are:\n\u000f\nReporting states for enabled conditions\n\u000f\nReporting state for clear\nDTC\nconditions\n\u000f\nReporting state for monitor results\nA detailed description of\nAPI\ns that cache the function and also about what is cached,\ncan be found in the individual chapters where these\nAPI\ns are described.\n7.4.4.2 Diagnostic Events\n7.4.4.2.1 Event Definition\nDiagnostic events are used by applications to report the state of a monitored entity\nto the\nDM\n.
