      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nDM\nto inform the AA about monitor state changes. From this perspective the interface\nis a provided port. This makes the\nara::diag::Monitor\ninterface different to other\nclasses and this is also the reason that\nara::diag::Monitor\nhas an\nara::diag::\nMonitor::Offer\nand\nara::diag::Monitor::StopOffer\nmethod that usually is\nonly available for provided ports.\nThe\nara::diag::Monitor::Offer\nmethod is necessary to provide an application\nthe possibility to inform the\nDM\nthat the application is ready to receive calls on the\nregistered notifier. The notifier is registered in the constructor of the\nara::diag::\nMonitor\nclass. The concrete instance of the monitor object is only known after the\nobject is created. As monitor class and the notifier instance are coupled (the notifier\nneeds to know for which monitor it is used) the application needs to tell its notifier for\nwhich monitor object it is created. Therefore after creation of the\nara::diag::Moni-\ntor\nclass is not active until\nara::diag::Monitor::Offer\nis called. Before\nara::\ndiag::Monitor::Offer\nis called, the application can complete the initialization of\nthe notifier by providing the notifier implementation with a reference to the monitor\nobject. Without this, the\nDM\ncould call the notifier immediately after the object is con-\nstructed into a notifier object, that would not be fully initialized from application point of\nview.\nThe\nara::diag::Monitor::StopOffer\nis the counterpart of the\nara::diag::\nMonitor::Offer\n. At shutdown it defines a point in time where the application re-\nquests the monitor object to be no longer used and after\nara::diag::Monitor::\nStopOffer\nit no longer expects calls on the notifier. After\nara::diag::Moni-\ntor::StopOffer\nthere are also no further calls on the corresponding\nara::diag::\nEvent::GetFaultDetectionCounter\nmethod. Without the\nara::diag::Moni-\ntor::StopOffer\nit would be undefined until when an application will receive calls on\nthe notifier and the notifier object could be safely discarded.\nTo avoid these kind of race conditions in object initialization/deinitialization the\nara::\ndiag::Monitor::Offer\nand\nara::diag::Monitor::StopOffer\nmethods are\nintroduced.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01112]\n{DRAFT}\nEvent memory entry for\nevents\nwith the combina-\ntion on storage\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticCommonProps\n.\ntypeOfEventCombinationSup-\nported\nis set to\neventCombinationOnStorage\n, then, the\nDM\nshall use the com-\nbined\nUDS DTC status bit\ntransitions as trigger source for the allocation of the\nevent memory\nentry, collection or update of the event related data.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04200)\n[SWS_DM_01113]\n{DRAFT}\nAging counter for combined events\nd\nIf\nDiagnostic-\nCommonProps\n.\ntypeOfEventCombinationSupported\nis set to\neventCombina-\ntionOnStorage\n, the\nDM\nshall calculate the aging counter based on the combined\nDTC status.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04200)\n7.4.4.2.3.2 Combination On Retrieval\nFor event combination on retrieval, the\nDM\nallocates the stored data per event in the\nsame way as if no event combination is used. The event combination is done on\ndata retrieval while reporting the\nevent\nrelated data via\nUDS\n. The positive response\nmessage for ReadDTCInformation contains the data of all stored events concatenated.\nThus, the length of the response message increases with each event that has stored\ndata for this\nDTC\n.\n[SWS_DM_01114]\n{DRAFT}\nData storage for event combination on retrieval\nd\nIf\nDi-\nagnosticCommonProps\n.\ntypeOfEventCombinationSupported\nis set to\nevent-\nCombinationOnRetrieval\n, the\nDM\nshall trigger the collection, update and storage\nof event related data per event.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04200, RS_Diag_04067)\n[SWS_DM_01115]\n{DRAFT}\nData reporting for event combination on retrieval\nd\nIf\nDiagnosticCommonProps\n.\ntypeOfEventCombinationSupported\nis set to\neventCombinationOnRetrieval\n, the\nDM\nshall return the event related data of all\nassigned events to\nUDS\nby concatenating the data of all events into one response for\nthe same\nDTC\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04200, RS_Diag_04067)\nThe aging and displacement of\nDTC\nwith event combination on retrieval is done in the\nsame way as for\nDTCs\nwith only one assigned event.\nWith event combination on retrieval the positive response of a\nUDS\nrequest to re-\ntrieve\nsnapshot records\nor extended data records contains the same record mul-\ntiple times.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nrecords and for one record number multiple\nevents\nhave data, the\nDM\nshall report the\nstored event data in chronological order of the event data storage with the oldest entry\nfirst.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04200)\n7.4.4.2.4 EnableConditions\nThe\nDM\nprovides also\nEnable Conditions\nto ignore a certain call of\nara::diag::\nMonitor::ReportMonitorAction\nin required situations.\nDiagnosticEnableCondition\ns are mapped to\nDiagnosticEvent\ns by\nDiag-\nnosticEventToEnableConditionGroupMapping\ns.\nEnable Conditions\nare controlled via the function\nara::diag::Condition::\nSetCondition\n. There current corresponding status, either '\nkConditionFalse\n'\nor\nkConditionTrue\ncan be retrieved via '\nara::diag::Condition::GetCondi-\ntion\n'.\n[SWS_DM_00568]\n{DRAFT}\nHandling of\nenable conditions\nd\nIf the function\nara::diag::Monitor::ReportMonitorAction\nis called and one or more of the\nevent assigned enable conditions are not fulfilled, the\nDM\nshall ignore the reported\nmonitor result.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04192)\nNote: For a regular processing of\nara::diag::Monitor::ReportMonitorAc-\ntion\nall\nof the\nenable conditions\nmapped to the corresponding\nevent\nhave to\nbe fulfilled.\nThe\nDM\nprovides two types of interfaces that can be used from an\nAA\nto set or get\nconditionstates. The\nara::diag::Condition\ninterface provides operations that are\nassigned for one single condition, that is mapped via\nDiagnosticEnableCondi-\ntionPortMapping\n. For each\nDiagnosticCondition\nthe\nAA\nneeds to instantiate\nexactly one\nara::diag::Condition\ninstance. The\nara::diag::MultipleCon-\ndition\nprovides the same functionality, but there is one interface that can be used\nfor multiple\nDiagnosticCondition\nelements. This is helpful for applications that\nare handling many conditions and the creation of a large amount of\nara::diag::\nCondition\ninterfaces would be an overhead. In that case a single interface can be\nused for many conditions and each operation provides a further conditionHandle as\nparameter to identify the condition for which the operation is applicable. Each\nDi-\nagnosticCondition\nrequires a mapping via\nDiagnosticMultipleCondition-\nPortMapping\nto express, that a multiple condition interface can be used for operation\non this condition.\nFunction wise both interfaces offer the same kind of operations and do have the same\nsemantics. For simplicity in this document the functionality of the condition class is\ndescribed only via\nara::diag::Condition\n. Whenever a functionality of the\nara::\ndiag::Condition\nclass is described, the same applies for the operation on the\nara::diag::MultipleCondition\n.\n187 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_01735]\n{DRAFT}\nMultipleCondition ConditionHandleType Generation\nd\nThe ConditionHandleType is a numerical value created by the following rules:\n\u000f\nIf no\nDiagnosticMultipleConditionPortMapping\n.\noverrideId\nexists, in\nalphabetical order of\nDiagnosticCondition\nshortname the\nDM\nassigns for the\nfirst\nDiagnosticCondition\na number of 0x010000 and increments this num-\nber for each further\nDiagnosticCondition\n.\n\u000f\nIf\nDiagnosticMultipleConditionPortMapping\n.\noverrideId\nexists, the\nnumber idOverride shall be used instead.\n\u000f\nIf an automatic created number collides with a preconfigured idOverride value,\nthe next free value shall be chosen.\nc\n()\nThe idOverride is used to allow the application developer or integrator to use/reuse\na fixed number from the application that is not changed if the auto generated num-\nber changes due to an update of the input configuration with new events or changed\nnames. The numbers are greater or equal to 0x010000, reserving the range between\n0x0000 and 0xFFFF for future extensions and definitions.\n[SWS_DM_01736]\n{DRAFT}\nInvalid ConditionHandleType\nd\nIf any\nara::diag::\nMultipleCondition\nmethod with input parameter conditionHandle is called and this\ninstance of MultipleCondition has not mapped\nDiagnosticMultipleCondition-\nPortMapping\nthat would create the provided ConditionHandleType, the\nDM\nshall re-\nturn\nkInvalidArgument\n.\nc\n()\n7.4.4.2.5 Debouncing\nDebouncing of reported\nevents\nis the capability of the\nDM\nto filter out undesirable\nnoise reported by\nmonitors\n. This is used to mature the result of the\nmonitor\n.\nDebouncing means that a report from a\nmonitor\ndoes not immediately lead to a\nchange of the\nEvent status\nbit \"\nkTestFailed\n\" but that a delaying threshold value\nmust be reached before. This results in the states for\nara::diag::Debounc-\ningState\n. If this threshold value is reached (\nFDC\n-equivalent is +127 (FDC\nmax\n) or -128\n(FDC\nmin\n)), the\nara::diag::DebouncingState\nis either\nkFinallyDefective\nor\nkFinallyHealed\n. This finally also leads than to a change of the\nEvent status\nbit\n\"\nkTestFailed\n\".\nThere are two kinds of different debounce algorithms implemented by the\nDM\n:\n\u000f\nCounter-based debouncing ( see 7.4.4.2.5.1 Counter-based debouncing))\n\u000f\nTime-based debouncing ( see 7.4.4.2.5.2 Time-based debouncing))\nBesides the here described debouncing algorithms within the\nDM\nimplementation, there\nis also the possibility to do the debouncing monitor-internal within the\nAA\n(compare\n188 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

But since this functionality is not part of the\nDM\n, this document just\ndescribes this use case in 7.4.4.2.5.3 Monitor-internal debouncing).\nIf the\nFDC\nfor an\nevent\nwith monitor-internal debouncing is needed, the regis-\ntered function parameter\ngetFaultDetectionCounter\nfrom the constructor\nara::\ndiag::Monitor::Monitor\nneeds to be used.\nWhich algorithm is used can be configured on a per\nevent\nbasis.\nThe DM is not supporting debouncing for an event:\n\u000f\nIf an event is not referenced by any\nDiagnosticEventToDebounceAlgo-\nrithmMapping\n.\ndiagnosticEvent\n\u000f\nIf an event is referenced by\nDiagnosticEventToDebounceAlgorithmMap-\nping\nand\nDiagnosticDebounceAlgorithmProps\n.\ndebounceAlgorithm\nis\nconfigured to\nDiagEventDebounceMonitorInternal\n.\nNote: [constr_10418] enforces the existence of attribute\nDiagnosticDebounceAl-\ngorithmProps\n.\ndebounceAlgorithm\n.\nA monitoring application will call the method\nara::diag::Monitor::ReportMon-\nitorAction\nwith the parameter\naction\nset to\nkPrepassed\nor\nkPrefailed\nfor\nevents, that are debounced by the\nDM\n.\nFor debouncing configuration values associated with diagnostic\nevents\n, two sources\ncan be referenced - 1)\nDEXT\n, 2) Monitor constructor. The debouncing configuration\nprovided to the Monitor constructor is considered as default and is overwritten if a\ndebouncing configuration is provided in\nDEXT\n. As a consequence, any debouncing\nconfiguration in\nDEXT\nneeds to have a meaningful value.\n[SWS_DM_01099]\n{DRAFT}\nDebouncing parameters from DEXT\nd\nIf Debouncing pa-\nrameters are present in\nDEXT\nand Debouncing Algorithm is fitting (i.e. Timer Based or\nCounter based),\nDM\nshall refer to the\nDEXT\nvalues as given in the requirements below\nand ignore any values derived from Monitor Constructors.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_01100]\n{DRAFT}\nDebouncing Algorithm not fitting\nd\nIf Debouncing pa-\nrameters are present in\nDEXT\nand Debouncing Algorithm is not fitting (Timer or Counter\nbased method is not configured appropriately),\nDM\nshall treat this as a Violation with\nthe following error message: \"Mismatching Debounce Algorithm in\nDEXT\n{modelledAl-\ngorithm} and runtime {ctorAlogrithm}\". {modelledAlgorithm} is the mapped debounce\nalgorithm according to DiagnosticEventToDebounceAlgorithmMapping, {ctorAlogrithm}\nis the algorithm that is chosen in the ctor.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_01101]\n{DRAFT}\nDebouncing parameters from Monitor Constructor\nd\nIf\nDebouncing parameters and methods are not present in\nDEXT\n,\nDM\nshall use the Monitor\nConstructor values and Algorithm, as provided. In these instances, debouncing rele-\nvant\nDEXT\nparameters in the following requirements shall be replaced by the Monitor\nConstructor values.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068)\n189 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.2.5.1 Counter-based debouncing\nCounter-based debouncing is done on a per\nevent\nbased counting policy of reported\nkPrepassed\nor\nkPrefailed\nfrom\ndiagnostic monitors\n. Per event an internal\ndebounce counter is used. Passed or failed event states for events are calculated by\nevaluating configured thresholds of the internal debounce counter.\n[SWS_DM_00014]\n{DRAFT}\nUse of counter-based debouncing for events\nd\nA\nDi-\nagnosticEvent\nshall be subject to counter-based debouncing if the\nDiagnos-\nticEvent\nis referenced in the role\ndiagnosticEvent\nby a\nDiagnosticEvent-\nToDebounceAlgorithmMapping\n, where the referenced\ndebounceAlgorithm\nag-\ngregates a\nDiagEventDebounceCounterBased\nin the role\ndebounceAlgorithm\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_00018]\n{DRAFT}\nInternal debounce counter init\nd\nUpon start-up, the\nDM\nshall initialize the event's internal debounce counter to '0'.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_00017]\n{DRAFT}\nCalculation of the FDC based on the internal de-\nbounce counter\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall calculate the\nFDC\naccording to UDS, based on the\nvalue and range of the internal debounce counter by linear mapping in order to achieve\na value range of -128 ... +127.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04125, RS_Diag_04190)\n[SWS_DM_00875]\n{DRAFT}\nInternal debounce counter incrementation\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall increment the event's internal debounce counter by the configured step-size value\nof\nDiagEventDebounceCounterBased\n.\ncounterIncrementStepSize\n, when the\nrelated\nmonitor\ncalls the method\nara::diag::Monitor::ReportMonitorAc-\ntion\nwith the parameter\naction\nset to\nkPrefailed\n. If after the incrementation the\ndebounce counter value is greater than the threshold\nDiagEventDebounceCoun-\nterBased\n.\ncounterFailedThreshold\n, the\nDM\nshall set the debounce counter value\nequal to the threshold.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04125, RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_00024]\n{DRAFT}\nQualified failed event using counter-based debounc-\ning\nd\nIf the internal debounce counter is greater or equal to\nDiagEventDebounce-\nCounterBased\n.\ncounterFailedThreshold\nthe\nDM\nshall process the event as\nkFi-\nnallyDefective\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04125, RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_00876]\n{DRAFT}\nInternal debounce counter decrementation\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall decrement the event's internal debounce counter by the configured step-\nsize value of\nDiagEventDebounceCounterBased\n.\ncounterDecrementStep-\nSize\n, when the related\nmonitor\ncalls the method\nara::diag::Monitor::Re-\nportMonitorAction\nwith the parameter\naction\nset to\nkPrepassed\n. If after the\ndecrementation the debounce counter value is lower than the threshold\nDiagEvent-\nDebounceCounterBased\n.\ncounterPassedThreshold\n, the\nDM\nshall set the de-\nbounce counter value equal to the threshold.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04125, RS_Diag_04068)\n[SWS_DM_00025]\n{DRAFT}\nQualified passed event using counter-based de-\nbouncing\nd\nIf the internal debounce counter is less or equal to\nDiagEventDebounce-\nCounterBased\n.\ncounterPassedThreshold\nthe\nDM\nshall process the event as\nkFi-\nnallyHealed\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04125, RS_Diag_04068)\n190 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00880]\n{DRAFT}\nDebounce time freeze request\nd\nIf the\nara::diag::\nMonitor::ReportMonitorAction\nmethod of a\nara::diag::Monitor\ninstance\nis called with the parameter\naction\nset to\nkFreezeDebouncing\n, for events with\nDi-\nagEventDebounceTimeBased\ndebouncing, the\nDM\nshall freeze the related debounce\ntimer of the corresponding\nevent\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04068, RS_Diag_04225)\nFreezing of the timer is only supported for events with\nDiagEventDebounceTime-\nBased\ndebouncing.\n[SWS_DM_00038]\n{DRAFT}\nContinuing a frozen debounce timer\nd\nIf a debounce\ntimer is frozen (i.e. the corresponding\nmonitor\nhas called\nara::diag::Monitor::\nReportMonitorAction\nwith the parameter\naction\nset to\nkFreezeDebouncing\n)\nand a new\nkPrepassed\nor\nkPrefailed\nis reported for this event, the\nDM\nmodule shall\ncontinue running the debounce timer starting with the frozen value.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04225)\n7.4.4.2.5.3 Monitor-internal debouncing\nMonitor-internal debouncing is completely left to the diagnostic monitor\nAA\nwhich just\nreports the final debouncing results by calling\nara::diag::Monitor::ReportMon-\nitorAction\non a per event base.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAt the time the application calls the\nara::diag::Condition::SetCondition\nmethod, the connection between the interface and the\nDM\nmight not be active. Typ-\nical situations are startup or communication interruptions. To ensure that no crucial\ndata is lost, the conditions interface is caching the result and bridges the time-span,\nuntil the connection to the\nDM\nis up and running again.\n[SWS_DM_01093]\n{DRAFT}\nCaching of conditions\nd\nIf the function SetCondition() is\ncalled and the\nDM\nis currently not ready to process the reported condition state, the\nDM\nshall cache the latest reported condition and evaluate it when the connection to the\nDM\nis (re-)established.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04192)\n7.4.4.4 Operation Cycles Management\nThe\nDM\nsupports operation cycles according to ISO 14229-1[1]. Operation cycles have\ndirect effect on the\nUDS DTC status byte\nand the event memory behavior.\nExamples of typical operation cycles are:\n\u000f\nIgnition on/off cycles\n\u000f\nPower up/power down cycle\n\u000f\nAccumulated operating time cycles\n\u000f\n...\nOperation cycles are managed by the\nAA\n, the\nDM\nis notified about the restart of an\nop-\neration cycle\nby using the API interface function\nara::diag::OperationCy-\ncle::RestartOperationCycle\n.\n[SWS_DM_01103]\n{DRAFT}\nCaching of RestartOperationCycle\nd\nIf the function\nara::diag::OperationCycle::RestartOperationCycle\nis called and the\nDM\nis currently not ready to process the reported restart of the\noperation cycle\n, the\nDM\nshall cache one reported\noperation cycle\nrestart and evaluate it when the con-\nnection to the\nDM\nis (re-)established.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04178, RS_Diag_04182)\n[SWS_DM_01104]\n{DRAFT}\nOperation Cycle restart\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall only restart\nop-\neration cycles\nafter the previous restart has been fully processed. In other words\nthis means that there is no\noperation cycle\nrestart queue.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04178)\n[SWS_DM_01105]\n{DRAFT}\nRestart OperationCycle during the processing of pre-\nvious call\nd\nIf the\nDM\nis still processing the previous\nara::diag::OperationCy-\ncle::RestartOperationCycle\ncall of the same\noperation cycle\n, the\nDM\nshall\nignore the current method call.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04178)\n[SWS_DM_01358]\n{DRAFT}\nConsecutive registration of notifier with Opera-\ntionCycle::SetNotifier()\nd\nIn case of a consecutive call of\nara::diag::Opera-\ntionCycle::SetNotifier\nof the corresponding\nara::diag::OperationCycle\ninstance,\nDM\nmodule shall overwrite the previous registered notifier.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04178,\nRS_Diag_04186)\n201 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5 Event memory\nThe\nevent memory\nis the database for faults detected by the system. It stores status\ninformation for\nevents\n,\nDTCs\nand\nDTC\nrelated data.\nThe term \"\nevent memory\n\", wherever used in this specification, refers to the term \"\nfault memory\n\" as specified in ISO 14229-1 [1]. The DM \"\nevent memory\n\" is com-\npliant to the \"\nfault memory\n\" in ISO.\nThere can be multiple\nevent memories\nhandled by the\nDM\n.\n[SWS_DM_00055]\n{DRAFT}\nSupported event memories\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support the\n\u000f\nprimary event memory\n\u000f\nup to 256\nuser-defined event memories\naccording to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04214, RS_Diag_04150)\n[SWS_DM_00911]\n{DRAFT}\nInstances of DTCInformation interface\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall\nlink each instance of the\nara::diag::DTCInformation\nclass with the mapped\nDiagnosticMemoryDestination\nreferenced by the corresponding\nDiagnos-\nticMemoryDestinationPortMapping\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04214, RS_Diag_04150)\n[SWS_DM_00056]\n{DRAFT}\nAvailability of the primary event memory\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall\nsupport the\nprimary event memory\nif a\nDTC\nexists having a\nDiagnosticMemo-\nryDestinationPrimary\nreferenced by its\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\ndi-\nagnosticMemory\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04150)\n[SWS_DM_00057]\n{DRAFT}\nAvailability of a user-defined event memory\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support the\nuser-defined event memory\nwith the number\nDiagnos-\nticMemoryDestinationUserDefined\n.\nmemoryId\nif a\nDTC\nexists having a\nDi-\nagnosticMemoryDestinationUserDefined\nwith that user-defined number ref-\nerenced by its\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\ndiagnosticMemory\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04214)\nThe size of the different\nevent memories\nis configurable by the DM configuration\nparameters.\n[SWS_DM_00920]\n{DRAFT}\nConfiguration of the event memory size\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall\nprovide\nevent memories\nof a size according to the configuration parameter\nDi-\nagnosticMemoryDestination\n.\nmaxNumberOfEventEntries\n, where each single\nevent memory entry is to be understood as the complete data set that belongs to a\nDTC\n,\nincluding counters, cycles,\nsnapshot records\nand\nextended data records\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04064)\nIf there are limitations to the event memory size, an overflow can occur as a conse-\nquence. Therefore the DM provides an overflow indication in case the\nevent memory\noverflow\noccurs and a\ndisplacement\nstrategy.\n202 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "source_page": 203,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5.1\nDTC\nIntroduction\nA diagnostic trouble code (\nDTC\n) defines a unique identifier mapped to a\ndiagnostic\nevent\nvia\nDiagnosticEventToTroubleCodeUdsMapping\n. The\nDTC\nis used by\ndiagnostics, including e.g.\nUDS\ncommunication with an external tester, to uniquely\nidentify data within the\nevent memory\ndatabase.\n[SWS_DM_00060]\n{DRAFT}\nSet of supported\nDTCs\nd\nThe existence of a\nDiagnos-\nticTroubleCodeUds\nindicates that the\nDM\nshall support this\nDTC\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04201)\nNote: Due to\nDM\nrestrictions the 'DiagnosticTroubleCodeObd' and 'DiagnosticTrouble-\nCodeJ1939' are not supported.\n7.4.4.5.1.1 Format\nThe\nDTC\nitself is a 3 byte value, that could have different interpretations.\n[SWS_DM_00058]\n{DRAFT}\nDTC\ninterpretation format\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall use one internal\nDTC\nformat interpretation that is defined in\nDiagnosticMemoryDestinationPri-\nmary\n.\ntypeOfDtcSupported\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04157)\nNote: Refers to [TPS_DEXT_01008] in [3].\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00059]\n{DRAFT}\nRestriction on supported\nDTC\nformat\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support the following literals from interpreted\nDiagnosticMemoryDestina-\ntionPrimary\n.\ntypeOfDtcSupported\n(see also [SWS_DM_00058])\n\u000f\niso11992_4\n\u000f\niso14229_1\n\u000f\nsaeJ2012_da\nFurther information about the format mapping is defined in [SWS_DM_00062].\nThe following literals are\nnot\nsupported by the\nDM\n:\n\u000f\niso15031_6\n\u000f\nsaeJ1939_73\nc\n(RS_Diag_04201)\n7.4.4.5.1.2 Groups\nBesides the term\nDTC\n, diagnostics uses\nDTC groups\nto address a range of single\nDTCs\n. A\nDTC group\nis defined by using a dedicated\nDTC\nvalue out of the range of\nvalid\nDTCs\nto identify the\ngroup of DTCs\n.\n203 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "source_page": 204,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nA definition of valid\nDTC groups\nis provided by ISO 14229-1 [1] - Annex D.1. The\nDTC\ngroup\nis used in diagnostic just as any other\nDTC\nvalue, the\nDM\ninternally resolves the\nDTC group\nand applies the requested operation to all\nDTCs\nof that group. The most\ncommon\nDTC group\nis the group of all DTCs, assigned to the\nDTC\nvalue 0xFFFFFF.\n[SWS_DM_00064]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of\nDTC\ngroups\nd\nThe existence of a\nDiagnos-\nticTroubleCodeGroup\nshall define the existence of the\nDTC group\nwith the\nDTC\nidentifier\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeGroup\n.\ngroupNumber\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117, RS_-\nDiag_04115)\nNote: Refers to [TPS_DEXT_03014] in [3].\n[SWS_DM_00065]\n{DRAFT}\nAlways supported availability of the group of all DTCs\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall provide by default the\nDTC group\n'GroupOfAllDTCs' assigned to the\nDTC\ngroup identifier 0xFFFFFF. This\nDTC\ngroup contains always all configured DTCs.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00082]\n{DRAFT}\nRestriction on the configuration of the\nDTC\ngroup GroupOfAllDTCs\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall ignore any configuration of a\nDiagnostic-\nTroubleCodeGroup\n.\ngroupNumber\nwith a value of 0xFFFFFF.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\nA configuration of the\nDTC\ngroup 0xFFFFFF via\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeGroup\n.\ngroupNumber\nis not required. Within the\nDM\nbasically all services and diagnostic\nrequests having a\nDTC\nas input parameter accept also\nDTC group\n. As result of this,\nthe operation is applied on all\nDTCs\nof that\nDTC group\n. To provide the reader a clear\nunderstanding if the\nDTC\nalso can be a\nDTC group\n, it is explicitly mentioned in this\nspecification. In case a\nDTC group\nis also valid, the\nDTC group\ndefinition of this\nchapter applies.\n7.4.4.5.1.3 Priority\nDTC priority is defined as a ranking based upon the level of importance. It is used\nto determine which entry may be removed from the\nevent memory\nin case the num-\nber of already stored events exceeds the maximum number of memory entries (event\nmemory is full) (7.4.4.5.10).\nIt is also used for\ninternal DiagnosticDataElement\ns connected to a\nDTCs ex-\ntended data record\n.\nEach supported\nDTC\nhas a priority assigned to it:\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\npriority\n;\n[SWS_DM_00916]\n{DRAFT}\nPriority values\nd\nIf a\nDTC\nhas a priority value of 1 and\ndisplacement\nneeds to be applied, the\nDM\nshall consider this as the highest priority.\nA higher value shall define a lower priority.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04118, RS_Diag_04071)\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00961]\n{DRAFT}\nLimits of priority values\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall only\nsupport\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\npriority\nvalues in the range of 1..255.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04118, RS_Diag_04071)\n204 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5.2 UDS DTC Status\n7.4.4.5.2.1 Status processing\nThe 'UDS DTC Status processing' is the\nDMs\nability to record and retain\nUDS\nstatus\nand associated interactions with other SW parts.\nThus the 'UDS Status processing' is an essential part of the\nDM\nfunctionality and is the\nsecond processing step after the\nEvent status\nhandling, as defined in 7.4.4.2.6.\nThe\nDM\nprovides means to other SW parts in order to control the\nUDS DTC status\nbits\n.\n[SWS_DM_00213]\n{DRAFT}\nDTC\nstatus processing\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall process the\nUDS DTC status byte\nharmonizing with the ISO 14229-1[1] standard.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04067)\nISO 14229-1 Annex D generally defines\nUDS DTC status byte\nhandling and the\ncorresponding triggerings for them. The following requirements map interfaces and\nconfiguration parameters of the\nDM\nto generic\nUDS DTC status bit\ntransition de-\nscriptions.\n[SWS_DM_00883]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS DTC status bit\ntransitions triggered by test\nresults\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall process the\nUDS DTC status byte\nbased on the\nEvent\nstatus\nbits.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04067)\n[SWS_DM_00217]\n{DRAFT}\nUDS DTC status bit\ntransitions triggered by Clear-\nDiagnosticInformation\nUDS service\nd\nIf the clearing of a\nDTC\nis triggered by the\nUDS service\n0x14\nClearDiagnosticInformation\n, the\nDM\nshall process the\nUDS DTC\nstatus byte\naccording to ISO 14229-1[1].\nc\n(RS_Diag_04180, RS_Diag_04067)\n[SWS_DM_00218]\n{DRAFT}\nkConfirmedDTC\n(Bit3) calculation\nd\nIf the\nkTest-\nFailed\nbit (Bit0) of the\nUDS DTC status bit\nhas a transition from 0 to 1, the\nDM\nshall set the\nkConfirmedDTC\nbit (Bit3), in case a\nDiagnosticEvent\n.\nconfir-\nmationThreshold\nis configured and the trip counter is equal to\nconfirmation-\nThreshold\n-1.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04136, RS_Diag_04067, RS_Diag_04151)\nThe trip counter is processed according to ISO 14229-1[1], Annex D2. The trip\ncounter is always increased by one at the end of any operation cycle with\nkTest-\nFailedThisOperationCycle\n(Bit1) set to 1. Or in other words, a\nconfirmation-\nThreshold\nvalue of 1 or no configured value confirms the\nDTC\nat the same time, the\ntest failed bit is set to 1.\nIf\nAging\nis supported for a\nDTC\n, the status is handled according to [SWS_DM_00243].\nIf there is an indicator mapped to the\nDTC\n, the \"\nkWarningIndicatorRequested\n\" bit\nis handled as described in section 7.4.4.5.2.4.\n[SWS_DM_01037]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior of not configured\nDiagnosticEvent\n.\ncon-\nfirmationThreshold\nd\nIf the optional parameter\nDiagnosticEvent\n.\nconfirma-\ntionThreshold\nis not configured, the\nDM\nshall use a default value of '1' for that\nparameter.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04067)\n205 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThis means that a confirmedDTC is set to '1' along with a reported\nkFailed\nmonitor\naction\nresult.\n7.4.4.5.2.2 UDS DTC Status change notifications\n[SWS_DM_01030]\n{DRAFT}\nObservability of the\nUDS DTC status byte\nd\nIf an\nAA\ncalls the function\nara::diag::DTCInformation::GetCurrentStatus\n(\ndtc\n), the\nDM\nshall provide the current status of the given\ndtc\nID from within the corresponding\nara::diag::DTCInformation\ninstance.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04183)\n[SWS_DM_01031]\n{DRAFT}\nNotification about UDS\nDTC\nstatus changes\nd\nIf the\nAA\nhas registered for a UDS\nDTC\nstatus change notification via the function\nara::\ndiag::DTCInformation::SetDTCStatusChangedNotifier\nof the correspond-\ning\nara::diag::DTCInformation\ninstance, the\nDM\nshall call this notifier on any\nUDS\nDTC\nstatus change for every single\nDTC\nmapped to this fault memory.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04183)\n[SWS_DM_01350]\n{DRAFT}\nConsecutive registration of notifier with SetDTCSta-\ntusChangedNotifier()\nd\nIn case of a consecutive call of\nara::diag::DTCInfor-\nmation::SetDTCStatusChangedNotifier\nof the corresponding\nara::diag::\nDTCInformation\ninstance,\nDM\nmodule shall overwrite the previous registered noti-\nfier.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04183)\n7.4.4.5.2.3 Suppress DTC reporting\nThis chapter describes the dynamic suppression of\nDTC\nduring runtime. A suppressed\nDTC\nis not visible for any tester and also not for internal\nAAs\n. The\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nwill not stop internal processing of a suppressed\nDTC\n. An use-\ncase could be to hide a\nDTC\nin a certain market by an\nAA\nat run time.\n[SWS_DM_01308]\n{DRAFT}\nFunctionality of SetDtcSuppression()\nd\nIf\nara::\ndiag::DTCInformation::SetDtcSuppression\nis called for a\nDTC\nand the\nUDS\nDTC status byte\nof that\nDTC\nis pendingDTC = 0 and confirmedDTC = 0, the\nDi-\nagnostic Server instance\nshall set the suppression status of the selected\nDTC\nto value of the parameter\nsuppressionStatus\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n[SWS_DM_01307]\n{DRAFT}\nPrecondition for suppression\nd\nIf\nara::diag::\nDTCInformation::SetDtcSuppression\nwith\nsuppressionStatus\n=\nkDTC-\nSuppressionOn\nis called for a\nDTC\nand the\nUDS DTC status byte\nof that\nDTC\nis\npendingDTC = 1 or confirmedDTC = 1, the suppression status shall remain unchanged\nand respond with\nkSuppressionIgnored\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n[SWS_DM_01306]\n{DRAFT}\nFunctionality of GetDtcSuppression()\nd\nIf\nara::\ndiag::DTCInformation::GetDtcSuppression\nis called, the\nDiagnostic\n206 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nara::diag::DTCInformation::GetNumberOfStoredEntries\nshall only\ncount non suppressed\nDTCs\n.\n\u000f\nara::diag::DTCInformation::Clear\nwith parameter\ndtcGroup\n\nis set to\nDTC group\n(including\nGroupOfAllDTCs\n) containing a suppressed\nDTC\nshall clear this suppressed\nDTC\n\nwhich is suppressed and different to any configured value of\nDiagnostic-\nTroubleCodeGroup\n.\ngroupNumber\nand has a value less than 0xFFFF00\n(defined range for functional group identifier), the\nDM\nshall trigger the error\nkWrongDtc\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n[SWS_DM_01299]\n{DRAFT}\nEnabling of the notification SetDTCStatusChanged-\nNotifier() for suppressed\nDTCs\nd\nIf\nara::diag::DTCInformation::SetDTCSta-\ntusChangedNotifier\nis called to enable the notification and the requested\nDTC\nis a\nsuppressed\nDTC\n, the\nDM\nshall return\nkNoSuchDTC\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n[SWS_DM_01298]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior of SetDTCStatusChangedNotifier() for sup-\npressed\nDTCs\nd\nIf a notification on status change is enabled and is caused by a sup-\npressed\nDTC\nthis notification shall be suppressed.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n[SWS_DM_01297]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior of SetNumberOfStoredEntriesNotifier() for\nsuppressed\nDTCs\nd\nIf a notification on number of stored fault memory entries change\nis enabled, a suppressed\nDTC\nshall not release a notification triggered by suppressing\nor unsuppressing a\nDTC\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\nAll other functions of interface\nara::diag::DTCInformation\nare not affected by a\nsuppressed\nDTC\n.\n[SWS_DM_01296]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior of service ResponseOnEvent with subfunc-\ntion onDTCStatusChange for suppressed\nDTCs\nd\nSuppressed\nDTCs\nshall not lead to\nserviceToRespondTo messages for service ResponseOnEvent(0x86) with subfunction\nonDTCStatusChange(0x01).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04220)\n7.4.4.5.2.4 Indicators\nIndicators can be associated with a particular\nDiagnosticEvent\n. Indicators or 'warn-\ning outputs' may consist of lamp(s), displayed text information or similar vendor specific\nexpressions. There can be various DiagnosticEvents per indicator and one\nDiagnos-\nticEvent\ncan have zero, one or more different indicators assigned.\nThe indicators are activated and deactivated based on the configured failure and heal-\ning cycles per Event.\n[SWS_DM_00888]\n{DRAFT}\nObservability of indicator status\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall provide\nthe status of an indicator via the function\nara::diag::Indicator::GetIndica-\ntor\nof the corresponding\nara::diag::Indicator\ninstance.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04204)\n208 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

\"WarningIndicatorRe-\nquested\" bit to 1 and set the healing counter to 0.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04204)\nFor confirmation check [SWS_DM_00218].\n[SWS_DM_01032]\n{DRAFT}\nHandling of 'WIR' bit without       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5.2.5 User controlled WarningIndicatorRequest-bit\nIn some cases (e.g. controlling a failsafe reaction in an application) the WIR-bit\n(WarningIndicatorRequest-bit) of a corresponding event in\nDM\nshall be set/reset by a\ndedicated \"fail-safe\nAA\n\".\nThe \"failsafe\nAA\n\" has to ensure a proper status of the WIR-bit (e.g. regarding to ISO-\n14229-1[2] or manufacture specific requirements).\nThe failsafe\nAA\nshall report the required WIR-status to\nDM\n(via the func-\ntion\nara::diag::Event::SetLatchedWIRStatus\nof the corresponding\nara::\ndiag::Event\ninstance) and has to ensure that the current WIR-status of an event\n(in\nDM\n) fits to the current fail-safe-status in the application:\n\u000f\nfail-safe reaction\nactive: WIR-bit shall be set to \"1\"\n\u000f\nfail-safe reaction\nnot active: WIR-bit shall be set to \"0\"\nThe fail-safe\nAA\nhas to report the status after every change of its fail-safe state.\nTherefore the\nDM\nprovides the function\nara::diag::Event::SetLatchedWIRSta-\ntus\nto set or reset the\nUDS DTC status bit\n\"\nkWarningIndicatorRequested\n\"\nof the related\nDTC\n.\nEach invocation of the function\nara::diag::Event::SetLatchedWIRStatus\nof\nan\nara::diag::Event\ninstance updates the WIR-bit for the corresponding\nDTC\nDue to not storing the Status-Bit 7 ('warningIndicatorRequested' bit) on Shutdown, the\nfail-safe\nAA\nhas to ensure that the 'warningIndicatorRequest' bit of a DTC fits to the\ncurrent failsafe status after initialization of the\nDM\n.\nSetting the WIR-bit of a DTC can be controlled via SetLatchedWIRStatus() OR by the\nDM internal WIR-bit handling. (OR-Operation).\n[SWS_DM_01033]\n{DRAFT}\nUser controlled set of WIR-bit\nd\nIf the function\nara::\ndiag::Event::SetLatchedWIRStatus\nis called with parameter\nstatus\n= TRUE,\nthe\nDM\nshall set the WIR-bit of the corresponding DTC to \"1\".\nc\n(RS_Diag_04204)\n[SWS_DM_01034]\n{DRAFT}\nUser controlled reset of WIR-bit\nd\nIf the function\nara::\ndiag::Event::SetLatchedWIRStatus\nis called with parameter\nstatus\n= FALSE\nand the DM internal WIR-bit handling is also not requesting it, the\nDM\nshall reset the\nWIR-bit of the corresponding event to \"0\".\nc\n(RS_Diag_04204)\n[SWS_DM_01035]\n{DRAFT}\nUser controlled WIR-bit handling and ControlDTCSet-\nting\nd\nIf ControlDTCSetting is set to disabled according to [SWS_DM_00910] and the\nfunction\nara::diag::Event::SetLatchedWIRStatus\nis called, the DM shall not\nchange the status of the WIR-bit and the function shall return\nkReportIgnored\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04204)\n210 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5.3 Destination\nEach\nDTC\nis stored in one of the supported\nevent memories\naccording to\n[SWS_DM_00056] and [SWS_DM_00057].\n[SWS_DM_00083]\n{DRAFT}\nEvent memory destination of an\nDTC\nd\nThe existence\nof\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\ndiagnosticMemory\nshall assign all DTCs ref-\nerencing this\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\nto the\nevent memory\nreferenced\nby\nDiagnosticTroubleCodeProps\n.\ndiagnosticMemory\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04150, RS_-\nDiag_04214)\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00084]\n{DRAFT}\nEach\nDTC\nshall be assigned to an event\nmemory destination\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall only support\nDTCs\nwith a configured\nDiagnos-\nticTroubleCodeProps\n.\ndiagnosticMemory\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04150, RS_Diag_04214)\n7.4.4.5.4\nDTC\nrelated data\nThe following sections deal with the\nDTC\nrelated data, what includes the triggering and\nlocation of freeze frames and extended data records to be stored to.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote that contrary to\nsnapshot records\n,\nextended data records\ndo not nec-\nessarily represent data collected in different points in time. Extended data consists of a\nconfigurable number of\nextended data records\n, which are all collected when the\nrespective memory entry is created in the event memory. The update mechanism of\nextended data records\nis configurable.\nAn\nextended data record\ntypically contains\nDM internal\ndata information. This\nis represented as\nDiagnosticDataElement\nreferenced from\nDiagnosticPro-\nvidedDataMapping\n, where the\ndataProvider\ndefines the content of the\ninter-\nnal\ndata. Such data elements can only be used within the scope of an\nextended\ndata records\n. The DEXT limits a use in other\nDiagnosticDataElement\nsuch as\nfrom\nsnapshot records\nor\nDiagnosticDataElement\nfrom\nDIDs\n.\n[SWS_DM_00155]\n{DRAFT}\nExtended data record numeration\nd\nExtended data\nrecord numbers shall always be determined by the configuration. The data layout\nof\nextended data record\nis defined by the order of\nDiagnosticExtended-\nDataRecord\n.\nrecordElement\n. Each\nDiagnosticDataElement\nshall be captured\nin its order via the corresponding read function instance for Typed DataElement:\nNamespace1OfPortInterface::Namespace2OfPortInterface::Short-\nnameOfDEPortInterface::Read\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04206, RS_Diag_04127)\n7.4.4.5.4.4 Internal statistical data elements in\nEDRs\nThe\nDM\nmodule provides the ability to map\ninternal data elements\n, like e.g.\naging counter, occurrence counter, ...       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.4.5.5 Clearing\nDTCs\nClearing a\nDTC\nor a\nDTC group\nis the ability of the\nDM\nto reset the\nUDS DTC sta-\ntus byte\nof each DTC and deleting\nDTC\nassigned\nsnapshot records\n,\nextended\ndata records\nand further\nDTC\n-related data.\n[SWS_DM_00116]\n{DRAFT}\nClearing a\nDTC group\nd\nWhen the\nDM\nis about to clear a\nDTC group\nit shall apply the same clear operation process as for a single\nDTC\non all\nthe\nDTCs\nof the\nDTC group\nwhich is cleared.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\n[SWS_DM_00117]\n{DRAFT}\nClearing a\nDTC\nd\nWhen the\nDM\nis about to clear a\nDTC\nit\nshall reset the event and\nUDS DTC status byte\nand clear the\nsnapshot records\nand\nextended data records\nstored for this\nDTC\nand its\nDTC\n-related data.\nc\n(RS_-\nDiag_04117)\n7.4.4.5.5.1 Locking of the\nDTC\nclearing process by a client\nThe\nDM\nsupports more than one\nDiagnostic Clients\nas described in section\n7.4.2.1.1. All configured clients can simultaneously send a ClearDTC diagnostic re-\nquest. This chapter describes the\nDM\nbehavior in this situations.\n[SWS_DM_00144]\n{DRAFT}\nParallel clearing DTCs in different\nDiagnosticMemo-\nryDestination\nd\nThe\nDM\nshall support parallel clearing of DTCs if the target of the\nclear\nDTC\noperation is a different\nDiagnosticMemoryDestination\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_-\n04117)\n[SWS_DM_00145]\n{DRAFT}\nAllow only one simultaneous clear\nDTC\noperation for\none\nDiagnosticMemoryDestination\nd\nIf a\nDiagnostic Client\nis clearing the\nDTCs of a\nDiagnosticMemoryDestination\nthe\nDM\nshall lock the clear\nDTC\nopera-\ntion for all other clients requesting to clear the DTCs of the same\nDiagnosticMemo-\nryDestination\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\n[SWS_DM_00146]\n{DRAFT}\nUnlock clear\nDTC\noperation for one\nDiagnosticMemo-\nryDestination\nd\nAfter the\nDM\nhas finished the clear\nDTC\noperation, it shall unlock the\nclear\nDTC\noperation for this\nDiagnosticMemoryDestination\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\n[SWS_DM_00147]\n{DRAFT}\nBehavior while trying to clear DTCs on a locked\nDi-\nagnosticMemoryDestination\nd\nIf the\nDM\nis requested to clear DTCs of a\nDiag-\nnosticMemoryDestination\nand the\nDM\nhas locked this\nDiagnosticMemoryDes-\ntination\nfor clearing DTCs according to [SWS_DM_00144], the\nDM\nshall refuse the\nsecond clear\nDTC\noperation and shall return a NRC 0x22 (ConditionsNotCorrect).\nc\n(RS_Diag_04117)\n218 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.28: Subfunctions of 0x19 / ReadDTCInformation with chronolicical reporting or-\nder\nc\n()\n[SWS_DM_00982]\n{DRAFT}\nReporting order direction\nd\nIf the\nDM\nmodule is requested\nto report in chronological order as specified in [SWS_DM_00981], the most recent\nevent memory\nentry shall be reported at first.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04195)\n7.4.5 Required Configuration\nThe Autosar Diagnostic Extract Template (DEXT) [3] is used for the DM configuration.\nBy design this format is made as exchange format between the tools in the diagnos-\ntic workflow, in different steps data is added. To accommodate the fact that data is\nincomplete and refined in a later step, the DEXT [3] allows most of the elements to\nbe optional and added at a later point in time. However at the point in time, when the\nDEXT [3] is used to configure the DM, a certain minimum content is required. In this\nchapter a loose list of DEXT [3] constraints is given. The mentioned elements need\nto be present so that the DM can be configured. Also the reaction on such missing\nelements is implementation specific, it is stated that the DM will not be able to behave\nas described in the document. A possible but not mandatory reaction is to refuse the\nDM generation at all and forcing the user to provide complete data.\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00168]\n{DRAFT}\nRequired operation cycles for diagnostic\nevents\nd\nEach\nDiagnosticEvent\nrequires exactly one\nDiagnosticEventToOper-\nationCycleMapping\nreferencing the\ndiagnosticEvent\nand one\nDiagnostic-\nOperationCycle\n.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04178)\n[SWS_DM_CONSTR_00206]\n{DRAFT}\nSupported format for data identifier for VIN-\nDataIdentifier\nd\nA\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nwith\nrepresentsVin\nset to true,\nrequires that it aggregates only one\nDiagnosticParameter\nwhich itself aggregates\na\nDiagnosticDataElement\nhaving a 17 byte uint8 array as\nbaseType\n.\nc\n(SRS_Eth_-\n00026)\n7.4.6 Diagnostic Data Management\nIn various situations, the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nfacilitates reading or writ-\ning of particular diagnostic data. One needs to distinguish between internal and ex-\nternal diagnostic data. By definition, internal data is managed by the\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nitself, and external data is managed by external applications. In\nthe latter case, communication between\nDiagnostic Server instance\nand the\n228 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nexternal application takes place via Service Interfaces. There are several Service In-\nterfaces defined concerning diagnostic data.\nThe purpose of this chapter is to describe the supported use-cases for handling diag-\nnostic data and the way how to configure each use-case within the\nDEXT\n.\nRecall that a\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nis composed of DiagnosticParameters\neach of which aggregates a single\nDiagnosticDataElement\n. In different use cases,\nit is required to manage diagnostic data either on the level of\nDiagnosticDataIden-\ntifier\nor on the fine granular level of DiagnosticDataElements.\n7.4.6.1 Internal and External Diagnostic Data Elements\nA\nDiagnosticDataElement\nis called\ninternal\nif there exists a\nDiagnosticPro-\nvidedDataMapping\nreferencing this\nDiagnosticDataElement\n, otherwise it is\ncalled an\nexternal DiagnosticDataElement\n.\nTable 7.29 gives a list of the supported\ninternal\nDiagnosticDataElements, where\nData Provider\nrefers to the NameToken defined by the attribute\ndataProvider\nof\nthe associated\nDiagnosticProvidedDataMapping\n,\nContent\ndescribes the actual content of the data,\nFormat\ndescribes the data format of the\nDiagnosticDataElement\n.\nContext\ndefines the exclusive context in which this\nDiagnosticDataElement\nis de-\nfined (if applicable). For \"DEM\" see\nDiagnostic Event Management\n. For\n\"DCM\" see\nDiagnostic Communication Management\n.\n[SWS_DM_01565]\n{DRAFT}\ninternaldataelements\nd"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00905]\n{DRAFT}\nRetrieving data for\nexternal\nDiagnosticDataEle-\nments\nd\nIf the\nDiagnostic Server instance\nis required to read data\nconfigured as\nexternal DiagnosticDataElement\n, then the\nDiagnostic\nServer instance\nshall utilize the associated\nRPortPrototype\ntyped by\nthe\nNamespace1OfPortInterface::Namespace2OfPortInterface::Short-\nnameOfDEPortInterface\nclass and call its\nNamespace1OfPortInterface::\nNamespace2OfPortInterface::ShortnameOfDEPortInterface::Read\nfunc-\ntion.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04097)\nNote: In general, there are multiple instances of\nNamespace1OfPortInterface::\nNamespace2OfPortInterface::ShortnameOfDEPortInterface\nclass avail-\nable in the running system. Which instance to choose for the given request to read\nan\nexternal DiagnosticDataElement\nis part of system integration. Support for\nthis integration is provided by DiagnosticMappings described in section 7.4.6.2.1.\n[SWS_DM_01275]\n{DRAFT}\nNamespace for typed DiagnosticDataElements in-\nterface\nd\nIf the typed DiagnosticDataElements interface is used, it shall fulfill\n[SWS_DM_00510] also.\nc\n(RS_Diag_04097)\n7.4.6.2 Reading and Writing Diagnostic Data Identifier\nThe\nDiagnostic Server instance\nsupports multiple ways to read or write diag-\nnostic data defined as\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\n:\n\u000f\nreading each\nDiagnosticDataElement\ncontained in the\nDiagnostic-\nDataIdentifier\nindependently as described in section 7.4.6.1,\n\u000f\nreading or writing the\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nas a whole via the\nDataIdentifier diagnostic interface,\n\u000f\nreading or writing the\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\nas a whole via the Gener-\nicService diagnostic interface.\nThe method to choose between these ways of data handling is by configuration of\nDiagnosticMappings referring to the\nDiagnosticDataIdentifier\n.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8 API specification\nThis chapter lists all provided and required C++ API interfaces of the\nDM\n. The C++ API\ninterfaces are divided into two parts:\n\u000f\nUDS Transportlayer interface\nA plug-in interface to extend the DM by own transport layers\n\u000f\nDiagnostic Application interface\nA\nDiagnosticPortInterface\ns is representing a corresponding code in-\nstance. The deployment is simplified due to a direct mapping to DiagnosticObject\nin DEXT.\n8.1 C++ language binding <sub component>\nNo content.\n8.2 API Common Data Types\n8.2.1 C++ Diagnostic Error Types\n[SWS_DM_00544]\n{DRAFT}\nUse of general ara::diag errors\nd\nAny\nChecked Error\nof a service interface shall be reported via the return type as specified in [6].\nc\n(RS_-\nAP_00128)\nIn\nara::diag\n, there are the following types of Checked Errors:\n1. Offer ara::diag errors: These errors can occur in a call of a any Offer interface\nmethod. They are defined in the error domain\nara::diag::DiagErrorDo-\nmain\n.\n2. Reporting ara::diag errors: These errors can occur in a call of a ReportMoni-\ntorAction interface method. They are defined in the error domain\nara::diag::\nDiagReportingErrorDomain\n.\n3. UDS NRC ara::diag errors: These errors can be returned by the skeletons. They\nare defined in the error domain\nara::diag::DiagUdsNrcErrorDomain\n.\n4. SOVD ara::diag errors: These errors can be returned by the skeletons for SOVD-\nspecific error reporting. They are defined in the error domain\nara::diag::\nDiagSovdErrorDomain\n.\nNote: Beside the AUTOSAR defined error domains, platform vendors can optionally\ndefine their own vendor specific error domains.\n236 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_DM_00561]\n{DRAFT}\nDeployment of diagnostic\nPortInterface\ns\nd\nDi-\nagnosticPortInterface\ns shall by default interact with the machine local DM.\nc\n(RS_AP_00114, RS_Diag_04097)\nNote: It is recommend to use ara::com as communication binding between the\nara::diag library and the DM process.\nNote: Platform vendors should optionally support a diagnostic deployment over ma-\nchine boundaries per process (i.e. the used communication binding should support\ncommunication across machines).\nThe\nAA\ncould instantiated specialzed\nDiagnosticPortInterface\ns for different pur-\nposes:\n\u000f\nDiagnosticRoutineInterface\nA typed interface for a single RoutineIdentifier\n\u000f\nDiagnosticRoutineGenericInterface\nA generic routine interface for multiple RoutineIdentifier(s)\n\u000f\nDiagnosticDataIdentifierInterface\nA typed data identifier interface for a single DataIdentifier\n\u000f\nDiagnosticDataIdentifierGenericInterface\nA generic data identifier interface for multiple DataIdentifier(s)\n\u000f\nDiagnosticDataElementInterface\nA typed data element interface for a single DataElement\n\u000f\nDiagnosticGenericUdsInterface\nA generic interface for diagnostic services\n\u000f\nDiagnosticMonitorInterface\nA interface for a single DiagnosticEvent\n8.3.1.2 MetaInfo class\nThe\nara::diag::MetaInfo\nclass specifies a mechanism to provide meta infor-\nmations, i.e. from transport protocol layer, to an interested application. To support\nthis,\nara::diag::MetaInfo::GetValue\nis specified, which provides the accord-\ning value represented as a\nara::core::StringView\n. The context of the current request\nmay also be retrieved by an application by calling\nara::diag::MetaInfo::Get-\nContext\n. The context of a request could be either\nkDiagnosticCommunication\n,\nkFaultMemory\nor\nkDoIP\n. The detailed information on meanings of the context and\nkey-value pairs can be looked up in Table 8.1 MetaInfo type definition.\n259 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_Diag_04135)\n8.3.2 C++ Diagnostic generated API Interfaces\nNamespaces are used to separate the definition of services from each other to prevent\nname conflicts and they allow to use reasonably short names.\n[SWS_DM_00510]\n{DRAFT}\nNamespace of Service header files\nd\nBased on the\nsym-\nbol\nattributes of the ordered\nSymbolProps\naggregated by\nPortInterface\nin role\nnamespace\n, the C++ namespace of the\nService header file\nshall be:\n1\nnamespace <PortInterface.namespace[0].symbol> {\n2\nnamespace <PortInterface.namespace[1].symbol> {\n3\nnamespace <...> {\n4\nnamespace <PortInterface.namespace[n].symbol> {\n5\n...\n6\n} // namespace <PortInterface.namespace[n].symbol>\n7\n} // namespace <...>\n8\n} // namespace <PortInterface.namespace[1].symbol>\n9\n} // namespace <PortInterface.namespace[0].symbol>\nwith all namespace names converted to lower-case letters.\nc\n(RS_AP_00114)\n8.3.2.1 Implementation Types header files\nThe\nImplementation Types header files\ninclude the ara::diag specific type declarations\nderived from the\nCppImplementationDataType\ns created from the definitions of\nAUTOSAR meta model classes within the\nDiagnosticPortInterface\ndescription.\n[SWS_DM_00511]\n{DRAFT}\nImplementation Types header files existence\nd\nThe\ndiagnostic management shall provide an\nImplementation Types header file\nfor\neach\nCppImplementationDataType\ndefined in the input by using the file name\n484 of 787 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_diag_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_D_P485_1153",
      "source_element": "SWS_DM_00512",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics",
      "source_page": 485,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Diagnostics\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nimpl_type_<symbol>.h\n, where\n<symbol>\nis the\nCpp Implementation Data Type\nsymbol\nconverted to lower-case letters.\nc\n(RS_AP_00116)\nThe\nImplementation Types header files\nmight need to include other header files, e.g.\nfor\nara::core::String\nor\nara::core::Vector\n.\n[SWS_DM_00512]\n{DRAFT}\nData Type definitions for AUTOSAR Data Types in Im-\nplementation Types header files\nd\nThe\nImplementation Types header files\nshall in-\nclude all the used definitions for types, structures and classes of the AUTOSAR Data\nTypes.\nc\n(RS_AP_00114)\n[SWS_DM_00513]\n{DRAFT}\nImplementation Types header file namespace\nd\nThe\nC++ namespace of the\nImplementation Types header file\nfor a given\nCppImple-\nmentationDataType\nis defined via the aggregated\nnamespace\n. Based on the\nsymbol\nattributes of the ordered\nSymbolProps\naggregated by\nCppImplementa-\ntionDataType\nin role\nnamespace\n, the C++ namespace of the\nImplementation Types\nheader file\nshall be:\n1\nnamespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[0].symbol> {\n2\nnamespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[1].symbol> {\n3\nnamespace <...> {\n4\nnamespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[n].symbol> {\n5\n...\n6\n} // namespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[n].symbol>\n7\n} // namespace <...>\n8\n} // namespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[1].symbol>\n9\n} // namespace <CppImplementationDataType.namespace[0].symbol>\nwith all namespace names converted to lower-case letters.\nc\n(RS_AP_00114)\n8.3.2.2 Typed Routine class\nThe\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nis only compatible with\nPortInterface\nof\nDiag-\nnosticRoutineInterface\n.\n[SWS_DM_00604]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API class Namespace1OfPortInter-\nface::Namespace2OfPortInterface::ShortnameOfRIPortInterface\nd"

Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Rolle des Diagnosemoduls</h4>\n<p><code>ara::diag</code> ist die Anwendungsoberfläche des Diagnostic Managers (DM): Anwendungen stellen Diagnosefunktionen bereit, während der DM UDS- und SOVD-Verkehr, Konversationszustand und Event-/DTC-Verarbeitung koordiniert. Ein Diagnostic Server wird pro <code>DiagnosticContributionSet</code> mit eigenen Ressourcen instanziiert; mehrere Instanzen teilen jedoch die UDS-Transport-Schicht <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00420\">[SWS_DM_00420]</a>. Damit ist die API nicht ein beliebiger UDS-Client, sondern die Rückruf- und Statusseite eines konfigurationsgebundenen Diagnostic Servers.</p>\n<h4>Anfrageweg und Servergrenzen</h4>\n<p>Der Transport Manager ordnet physisch adressierte UDS-Anfragen genau dem Server mit passender Diagnoseadresse zu, funktionale Anfragen dagegen allen passenden Serverinstanzen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00390\">[SWS_DM_00390]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00391\">[SWS_DM_00391]</a>. DoIP ist ein möglicher Transportkontext; die Spezifikation verlangt bei entsprechender Konfiguration eine an ISO 13400-2 ausgerichtete DoIP-Unterstützung <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2\">SWS Diagnostics §7.1.2 „DoIP“</a>. Der Diagnostic Server leitet daraus den einbyteigen NRC ab und sendet eine negative UDS-Antwort; für <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_diag_GenericUDSService_733cac.html\"><code>GenericUDSService::HandleMessage</code></a> ist ausdrücklich ein anwendbarer NRC vorgesehen. Die vom DM akzeptierten Rückgabewerte liegen im Bereich <code>0x01</code> bis <code>0xFE</code>. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.3.2.6.1\">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6.1 „NRCs created by application“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02059\">[SWS_DM_02059]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02060\">[SWS_DM_02060]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00618\">[SWS_DM_00618]</a></p>\n<p>Benötigt die Bearbeitung länger als der P2/P2*-Timer der aktuellen Session zulässt, erzeugt der Diagnostic Server die negative Antwort <code>0x78</code> (<code>kRequestCorrectlyReceivedResponsePending</code>). Er darf diese Rückmeldung bis zum Dienstabschluss wiederholen; erreicht ihre Anzahl dagegen den konfigurierten Grenzwert <code>maxNumberOfRequestCorrectlyReceivedResponsePending</code>, muss er die interne oder externe Bearbeitung abbrechen und <code>0x10</code> (<code>kGeneralReject</code>) senden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.2.6\">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6 „UDS response handling“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" in eine negative UDS-Antwort und verwaltet die Response-Pending-Grenzen selbst. Quellen: <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.2.6\">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6 „UDS response handling“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.3.2.6.1\">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6.1 „NRCs created by application“</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00368\">[SWS_DM_00368]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00369\">[SWS_DM_00369]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02060\">[SWS_DM_02060]</a>.</p>\n<p>Für lokale API-Fehler ist <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_diag_DiagErrorDomain_3f58d2.html\"><code>DiagErrorDomain</code></a> über seinen Alias <code>Errc</code> an <code>DiagErrc</code> gebunden. Dazu gehören unter anderem <code>kConfigurationMismatch</code>, <code>kReportIgnored</code>, <code>kInvalidArgument</code>, <code>kNotOffered</code>, <code>kBusy</code>, <code>kFailed</code>, <code>kMemoryError</code> und <code>kServiceNotAvailable</code>. Den Offer-Pfad trennt die Spezifikation davon: Ein zweiter Aufruf von <code>Offer()</code> liefert <code>DiagOfferErrc::kAlreadyOffered</code>. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00514\">[SWS_DM_00514]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00518\">[SWS_DM_00518]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00619\">[SWS_DM_00619]</a></p>\n<p>Im Eventpfad gibt <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_diag_Monitor_5df579.html\"><code>Monitor::Offer()</code></a> denselben Offer-Fehler zurück; <code>ReportMonitorAction()</code> hat hingegen keinen Rückgabewert. Eine zur konfigurierten Entprellungsart nicht unterstützte <code>MonitorAction</code> ist als <code>UnexpectedMonitorActionHandlingViolation</code> spezifiziert. Ist eine für die Dienstbearbeitung benötigte, offerpflichtige <code>ara::diag</code>-Schnittstelle nicht oder nicht mehr angeboten, antwortet der DM gegenüber dem Tester mit <code>0x94</code> (<code>kResourceTemporarilyNotAvailable</code>). <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01088\">[SWS_DM_01088]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00543\">[SWS_DM_00543]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01257\">[SWS_DM_01257]</a></p>\n<p>Auf der UDS-Transportgrenze bestätigt die Transportimplementierung das endgültige Netzwerkergebnis über <code>UdsTransportProtocolMgr::TransmitConfirmation</code>: Bei nicht übertragbarer UDS-Antwort ist das Ergebnis <code>kTransmitFailed</code>, andernfalls <code>kTransmitOk</code>. Damit ist ein Übertragungsfehler von einer negativen UDS-Antwort getrennt. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.1.1.3\">SWS Diagnostics §7.1.1.3 „UDS message transmission on a UDS TransportLayer“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00350\">[SWS_DM_00350]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00351\">[SWS_DM_00351]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00312\">[SWS_DM_00312]</a></p>\n<h4>Implementierungsleitlinien</h4>\n<ul><li>Callback-Interfaces mit <code>MetaInfo</code> dürfen dieses Objekt nur während des aktiven Aufrufs verwenden; Speichern oder Wiederverwenden ist nicht zulässig <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01345\">[SWS_DM_01345]</a>.</li><li>Für vom DM aufgerufene Anwendungsschnittstellen beschreibt <code>ConcurrencyType</code>, ob der DM parallele Callbacks ausführen darf; bei <code>kNotConcurrent</code> wartet er auf das finale Ergebnis <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.1\">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.1 „Interaction between DM and applications“</a>.</li><li>Die generischen DID- und Routine-Schnittstellen sind nur dort passend, wo die DEXT-Konfiguration sie einer Diagnosefunktion zuordnet. Die sichtbaren Platzhalternamen wie <code><RoutineInterface6>StartOutput</code> sind gewollte PDF-/Template-Artefakte und keine zur Laufzeit zu erzeugenden Typnamen.</li></ul><p Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Rolle des Diagnosemoduls</h4>
<p><code>ara::diag</code> ist die Anwendungsoberfläche des Diagnostic Managers (DM): Anwendungen stellen Diagnosefunktionen bereit, während der DM UDS- und SOVD-Verkehr, Konversationszustand und Event-/DTC-Verarbeitung koordiniert. Ein Diagnostic Server wird pro <code>DiagnosticContributionSet</code> mit eigenen Ressourcen instanziiert; mehrere Instanzen teilen jedoch die UDS-Transport-Schicht <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00420">[SWS_DM_00420]</a>. Damit ist die API nicht ein beliebiger UDS-Client, sondern die Rückruf- und Statusseite eines konfigurationsgebundenen Diagnostic Servers.</p>
<h4>Anfrageweg und Servergrenzen</h4>
<p>Der Transport Manager ordnet physisch adressierte UDS-Anfragen genau dem Server mit passender Diagnoseadresse zu, funktionale Anfragen dagegen allen passenden Serverinstanzen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00390">[SWS_DM_00390]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00391">[SWS_DM_00391]</a>. DoIP ist ein möglicher Transportkontext; die Spezifikation verlangt bei entsprechender Konfiguration eine an ISO 13400-2 ausgerichtete DoIP-Unterstützung <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Diagnostics §7.1.2 „DoIP“</a>. Die UDS-Behandlung läuft anschliessend als Diagnosekonversation und ruft je nach Service spezialisierte oder generische <code>ara::diag</code>-Interfaces auf.</p>

<h4>Konversation, Zugriff und Dienstbehandlung</h4>
<p>Eine <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_Conversation_8b92b3.html"><code>Conversation</code></a> repräsentiert den Laufzeitdialog eines durch Quelladresse und globalen Kanal identifizierten Clients mit einem Diagnostic Server <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00421">[SWS_DM_00421]</a>. Darin werden Session, Security-Level und Aktivität sichtbar. Die Klasse <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_SecurityAccess_b489ef.html"><code>SecurityAccess</code></a> stellt die Seed/Key-Callbacks für UDS 0x27 bereit; <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_GenericUDSService_733cac.html"><code>GenericUDSService</code></a> ist der Erweiterungspunkt für konfigurierte Custom-Diagnostic-Services.</p>

<h4>Event- und Fehlerspeicherpfad</h4>
<p>Für die Fehlerüberwachung meldet eine Anwendung über <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_Monitor_5df579.html"><code>Monitor</code></a> qualifizierte Monitoraktionen. <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_Condition_b614dc.html"><code>Condition</code></a> und <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_OperationCycle_67d05f.html"><code>OperationCycle</code></a> liefern die Umgebungs- bzw. Zyklusbedingungen. <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_DTCInformation_3c3d92.html"><code>DTCInformation</code></a> macht daraus resultierende DTC-Status-, Speicher- und Löschinformationen verfügbar <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.4">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.4 „Diagnostic Event Management“</a>.</p>

</div><p class="diagram-note">Zusammenhang der Event-Verarbeitung: Bedingungen steuern die Monitorbewertung; Monitoraktionen und Operation-Cycles beeinflussen Event- und DTC-Zustände. Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.3.4.1.2">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.4.1.2 „Monitors“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.4.3">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.4.3 „Operation Cycles Management“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.4.4">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.4.4 „Event memory“</a>. <em>Teilweise Interpretation: Die Darstellung fasst mehrere spezifizierte Verantwortlichkeiten als Objektzusammenarbeit zusammen.</em></p>
<h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p>Ein anwendungsspezifischer UDS-Service meldet eine fachlich negative Dienstbehandlung über den Fehlerkanal seines <code>Future</code> mit einem <code>ErrorCode</code> aus <code>DiagUdsNrcErrorDomain</code> beziehungsweise <code>DiagUdsNrcErrc</code>. Der Diagnostic Server leitet daraus den einbyteigen NRC ab und sendet eine negative UDS-Antwort; für <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_GenericUDSService_733cac.html"><code>GenericUDSService::HandleMessage</code></a> ist ausdrücklich ein anwendbarer NRC vorgesehen. Die vom DM akzeptierten Rückgabewerte liegen im Bereich <code>0x01</code> bis <code>0xFE</code>. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.3.2.6.1">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6.1 „NRCs created by application“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02059">[SWS_DM_02059]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02060">[SWS_DM_02060]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00618">[SWS_DM_00618]</a></p>
<p>Benötigt die Bearbeitung länger als der P2/P2*-Timer der aktuellen Session zulässt, erzeugt der Diagnostic Server die negative Antwort <code>0x78</code> (<code>kRequestCorrectlyReceivedResponsePending</code>). Er darf diese Rückmeldung bis zum Dienstabschluss wiederholen; erreicht ihre Anzahl dagegen den konfigurierten Grenzwert <code>maxNumberOfRequestCorrectlyReceivedResponsePending</code>, muss er die interne oder externe Bearbeitung abbrechen und <code>0x10</code> (<code>kGeneralReject</code>) senden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.2.6">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6 „UDS response handling“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00368">[SWS_DM_00368]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00369">[SWS_DM_00369]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00526">[SWS_DM_00526]</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Der Diagnostic Server übersetzt den NRC-Fehler der Anwendung in eine negative UDS-Antwort und verwaltet die Response-Pending-Grenzen selbst. Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.3.2.6">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6 „UDS response handling“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.3.2.6.1">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.2.6.1 „NRCs created by application“</a>, <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00368">[SWS_DM_00368]</a>, <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00369">[SWS_DM_00369]</a>, <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_02060">[SWS_DM_02060]</a>.</p>
<p>Für lokale API-Fehler ist <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_DiagErrorDomain_3f58d2.html"><code>DiagErrorDomain</code></a> über seinen Alias <code>Errc</code> an <code>DiagErrc</code> gebunden. Dazu gehören unter anderem <code>kConfigurationMismatch</code>, <code>kReportIgnored</code>, <code>kInvalidArgument</code>, <code>kNotOffered</code>, <code>kBusy</code>, <code>kFailed</code>, <code>kMemoryError</code> und <code>kServiceNotAvailable</code>. Den Offer-Pfad trennt die Spezifikation davon: Ein zweiter Aufruf von <code>Offer()</code> liefert <code>DiagOfferErrc::kAlreadyOffered</code>. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00514">[SWS_DM_00514]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00518">[SWS_DM_00518]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00619">[SWS_DM_00619]</a></p>
<p>Im Eventpfad gibt <a class="vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_diag_Monitor_5df579.html"><code>Monitor::Offer()</code></a> denselben Offer-Fehler zurück; <code>ReportMonitorAction()</code> hat hingegen keinen Rückgabewert. Eine zur konfigurierten Entprellungsart nicht unterstützte <code>MonitorAction</code> ist als <code>UnexpectedMonitorActionHandlingViolation</code> spezifiziert. Ist eine für die Dienstbearbeitung benötigte, offerpflichtige <code>ara::diag</code>-Schnittstelle nicht oder nicht mehr angeboten, antwortet der DM gegenüber dem Tester mit <code>0x94</code> (<code>kResourceTemporarilyNotAvailable</code>). <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01088">[SWS_DM_01088]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00543">[SWS_DM_00543]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01257">[SWS_DM_01257]</a></p>
<p>Auf der UDS-Transportgrenze bestätigt die Transportimplementierung das endgültige Netzwerkergebnis über <code>UdsTransportProtocolMgr::TransmitConfirmation</code>: Bei nicht übertragbarer UDS-Antwort ist das Ergebnis <code>kTransmitFailed</code>, andernfalls <code>kTransmitOk</code>. Damit ist ein Übertragungsfehler von einer negativen UDS-Antwort getrennt. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.1.1.3">SWS Diagnostics §7.1.1.3 „UDS message transmission on a UDS TransportLayer“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00350">[SWS_DM_00350]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00351">[SWS_DM_00351]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_00312">[SWS_DM_00312]</a></p>
<h4>Implementierungsleitlinien</h4>
<ul><li>Callback-Interfaces mit <code>MetaInfo</code> dürfen dieses Objekt nur während des aktiven Aufrufs verwenden; Speichern oder Wiederverwenden ist nicht zulässig <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=SWS_DM_01345">[SWS_DM_01345]</a>.</li><li>Für vom DM aufgerufene Anwendungsschnittstellen beschreibt <code>ConcurrencyType</code>, ob der DM parallele Callbacks ausführen darf; bei <code>kNotConcurrent</code> wartet er auf das finale Ergebnis <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.1">SWS Diagnostics §7.3.1 „Interaction between DM and applications“</a>.</li><li>Die generischen DID- und Routine-Schnittstellen sind nur dort passend, wo die DEXT-Konfiguration sie einer Diagnosefunktion zuordnet. Die sichtbaren Platzhalternamen wie <code><RoutineInterface6>StartOutput</code> sind gewollte PDF-/Template-Artefakte und keine zur Laufzeit zu erzeugenden Typnamen.</li></ul><p
